# Changelog

## [v1.9.81] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- Banned-class model locks (a 404 NOT_FOUND and its siblings — the upstream says the account does not have the model) now store a durable `modelGone_<model>` twin alongside the ordinary lock. The usage auto-release, which clears every `modelLock_` key whenever a quota read shows availability, used to resurrect those models within minutes, so a combo retried a disowned model hundreds of times per account; it can now only lift transient quota locks. Gone locks end by expiry, by a proven success on the pair, or by an explicit operator reset/unlock. Selection, the availability census, and the dashboard lock readers treat the durable twin as a lock.
- Orphan tool results are dropped in both request repairs: `EnsureToolCallIDs` (Claude→OpenAI) no longer forwards a tool message whose id names no tool call in the request, and `SanitizeClaudePassthrough` drops `tool_result` blocks no surviving `tool_use` claims. A result whose call fell out of the client's history (compaction cut, lane switch) made strict Claude-format upstreams refuse the whole request ("tool result's tool id ... not found").

## [v1.9.80] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- Mixed-provider histories still poisoned MiniMax after fragment 1066 (live storm continued post-v1.9.79; the tool-definition sanitizer was necessary but not the active poison). The fleet's real histories — replayed verbatim through the gateway to prove it — carry tool ids minted on the Gemini lane in the gateway's own transport form, `call_<n>__ts__<base64 thought signature>`, whose `/`, `+` and `=` characters fail the Messages API id charset. Claude-shaped bodies pass those ids through untouched, so MiniMax refused whole requests with "tool result's tool id(...) not found" (and sibling 2013 shapes), while two conversion paths additionally let a non-object tool_use input through ("tool_use.input: Input should be a valid dictionary"). SanitizeClaudePassthrough now normalizes every tool_use.id / tool_result.tool_use_id via cleanClaudeToolID: strip the `__ts__` transport suffix (the clean base id is the Gemini lane's own form, and the signature stays recoverable from the thought-signature store by that id), otherwise apply the deterministic sha rewrite the OpenAI→Claude converter already used. The translator's OpenAI→Claude message conversion applies the same id cleanup on its passthrough branches and its tool envelope, and both OpenAI→Claude converters now coerce a non-object parsed arguments value to the empty object instead of emitting it as a tool_use input. Verified by replay: a real 141-message fleet history that was refused with the tool-id error is accepted once its ids are normalized, and the gateway now performs that normalization itself.

## [v1.9.79] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- One malformed client tool definition could take down every MiniMax turn of a mixed combo (live storm 2026-11-09 22:10–22:21 WIB: 455 requests, ~3,700 attempts, all streaming /v1/messages via a combo, all refused by MiniMax with 2013 invalid-params while lenient members tolerated the same payload and were simultaneously quota/404-unavailable). MiniMax's Anthropic endpoint validates tool definitions strictly — a definition with an empty name returns "function name is empty", one with a missing/non-object schema returns "function parameters is empty" (both reproduced verbatim through the gateway) — where other upstreams shrug the same definitions off. SanitizeClaudePassthrough now repairs the tools array on the Claude passthrough path: definitions with a blank name are dropped (a nameless tool is uncallable in every dialect) and client tools (type custom or absent) whose input_schema is missing or not an object get the minimal object schema; server tools keep their shape. The OpenAI→Claude conversion (claudeToolsFromOpenAI) applies the same two rules so it cannot mint a definition the passthrough would have dropped.

### Fixed
- Model-availability census silently skipped connections whose per-model locks live only in flattened keys (audit 2026-11-09: of 41 census locks only 20 matched the DB; anaking966, abahakunan and adenarere held live locks yet never appeared in GET /api/models/availability at all). The Go-side reader (activeModelLocks) already unions the `modelLocks` object with the flattened `modelLock_<model>` keys, but the repo prefilter in GetLockedOrUnavailableConnections selected rows on the object alone — and writers store locks almost exclusively as flattened keys, the object routinely absent. The prefilter now also matches any row carrying a `modelLock_*` key, so the census enumerates the same locks the serving path enforces; no stored data changes.

## [v1.9.78] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- Quota Tracker verification UI never rendered at all (found by live browser verification of fragment 1063, 2026-11-09): the tracker's `isValidationFlagged` keyed only on the stored status flag, but the tracker's own list payload (`GET /api/providers/client`) folds a parked validation row into `effectiveStatus: 'disabled'` with `status: 'disabled'` — the canonical status engine has no validation verdict — so the predicate could never match on this surface and the strip from fragment 1063 (like the check control from fragment 1061 before it) stayed dead. The provider detail page was unaffected because its health derivation already carried the fallback.
- `isValidationFlagged` now mirrors connectionHealth's derivation: the stored flag, or a disabled effective status whose stored error carries the validation markers (`validation_required`, `verify your account`) — both fields are present on the client-page payload. The fragment-1062 prune inherits the corrected predicate, so a released account's strip still clears itself on refresh while a still-gated account's strip now actually appears.

## [v1.9.77] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- Quota Tracker verification UI parity with the provider detail page (owner request, 2026-11-09). A validation-flagged account's tracker card carried no "needs verification" badge at all, and its labeled "Verifikasi Akun" control existed only inside the card body's error and quota-message branches — a flagged card that rendered quota rows (or was still loading) offered nothing but a muted fact_check icon in the header action cluster.
- The card body now opens with an unconditional verification strip for every flagged connection: the amber "needs verification" badge (same treatment as the provider detail row) plus the Verifikasi Akun control — the check itself until a test mints a fresh URL, then the fresh-URL link, exactly the fragment-1061 shape. The two branch-local copies and the header icon button are removed, so the strip is the single verification control on the card; the fragment-1062 prune keeps it clearing itself when refreshed data drops the flag.

## [v1.9.76] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- Dashboard verification panels no longer outlive the flag they belong to. Since fragment 1061, a flagged row's Verifikasi test keeps the refusal's fresh verification URL in component state (never stored server-side) and the panel renders from that state; but when the account was released by a path the open page did not start — the usage auto-check enabling it server-side — refreshed row data alone never cleared the panel, so the operator kept seeing a verification warning for an account that was already active until they pressed Verifikasi again or reloaded (observed live 2026-11-09, anaking966: three Verifikasi presses landed before the 21:12 release, the warning stayed on screen after it).
- Provider detail view: an effect now prunes the per-row fresh-URL state whenever the health derivation over refreshed connections stops reading "validation" for that connection. Quota Tracker: the same prune keyed on its stored-flag check over its refreshed connection list. Entries for connections absent from the refreshed slice are left untouched — absence is not a verdict — and a still-gated account keeps its URL, because its refreshed row still carries the flag.

## [v1.9.75] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed
- Antigravity verification flow rebuilt around how Google's verification link actually behaves (proven live 2026-11-09): the link's plt token is minted per refusal and only resolves while the operator's browser holds a live sign-in session for the account, so a stored link is a dead letter by click time. The verification URL is never stored anymore: `SetConnectionVerificationRequired` records only the flag (`status=validation_required`, parked) and scrubs any legacy stored URL; every flagging path (chat classifiers, quota classification, list sweeper, validation recheck) writes the flag only.
- The connection test is the Verify action: for Antigravity it decides on a real pinned generate, not the light account probe. A still-gated verdict returns the refusal's fresh verification URL in the test response (response-only, never persisted); a verdict without the gate — success or any other upstream answer — enables the account in the same call. Fresh, unflagged Antigravity accounts get the same generate verdict, so a just-connected account that was born gated is caught by the connect flow itself.
- The Antigravity OAuth exchange no longer reactivates a validation-flagged connection on re-login (the sign-in-as-verification theory, falsified live 2026-11-09): it preserves the flag and the parked state, and the post-exchange test decides.
- Dashboard: the connect modal stays open on a Step 3 verification step (fresh URL field, Open, Copy, Check) when the post-exchange test finds the account gated; a flagged row's Verifikasi test surfaces the fresh URL in its error panel; the Quota Tracker's stored-link anchors became Verify actions with the same fresh-URL swap. Connection payloads no longer serve a stored `verificationUrl`, and health derivation keys off the stored status flag.

## [v1.9.74] - 2026-11-09

## Validation recheck: an upstream answer without the gate releases the account (v1.9.74)

- **Proven live (2026-11-09, nganzgore):** the owner completed Google's scan verification from the agy-printed link (QR scanned on his phone → "Authentication successful"); agy then served the account on its EXISTING token with no re-login — the scan lifts the gate account-side, settling the mechanism (both sign-in theories falsified). Server read-back minutes later: `loadCodeAssist` FULL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK returns currentTier=free-tier with ineligibleTiers EMPTY, and generate answers 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (quota), not 403 VALIDATION_REQUIRED.
- **Defect:** the gateway row stayed parked as validation_required. `recheckValidationFlag` treated every ping failure alike: a 429 answer re-parked the account with the stale verification verdict, so the owner's Verifikasi test button could never release an account whose verification was already done but whose quota was momentarily exhausted.
- **Fix:** in the recheck's failure branch, an upstream answer (`*proxy.UpstreamError` with a body) that does NOT carry the validation markers is itself the verdict — Google evaluated the generate and refused it for another reason, so the verification gate is gone and the account releases (the temporary release already left the row clean). A ping with no upstream answer (transport/timeout) still re-parks, and a still-gated refusal still re-parks with the fresh message + verification URL from that error, per the owner's Verifikasi-button spec (fragment 1059).
- **Verification:** go build + vet at release; live proof on staging — the connection test on nganzgore releases the row (read-back of isActive/status) while its generate still answers 429 quota.

## [v1.9.73] - 2026-11-09

## Antigravity verification: the Verifikasi button test-calls the completion API (v1.9.73)

- **Owner's spec (2026-11-09):** "verifikasi button itu langsung test call api completion. kalo gagal masih kena verif update url verifikasi nya" — the Verifikasi button must fire a real completion test for the account, and when the test still hits the verification gate, the verification URL must be updated from that test.
- **Backend already implements both halves** (`recheckValidationFlag`, v1.9.63/64): the verdict is a real pinned generate through the chat lane — a pass releases the account; a still-flagged failure re-parks it with the fresh `validation_url` extracted from that error's own body (`validationURLFromBody`; the plt token rotates per error, so the freshest always wins).
- **Change (UI wiring only):** the flagged row's primary action is now that test call, labelled **verifikasi** (spinner while running, row refresh on completion so the error panel's "Buka Verifikasi" link carries the URL the test just minted). The separate duplicate "recheck" button in the same state is removed — one action, the owner's name for it. The bare verification link remains only as "Buka Verifikasi" in the error panel.
- **Verification:** build + svelte-check gates at release; staging /api/version read-back after deploy.

## Antigravity verification panel: drop the scan note (v1.9.73)

## [v1.9.72] - 2026-11-09

## Antigravity verification: the scan verifies, not a sign-in — bundled button reverted (v1.9.72)

- **Owner's verdict (2026-11-09, after testing v1.9.71 himself):** "logika verifikasi = login ulang itu salah besar, gw udah login ulang pun percuma — yang harus diverifikasi itu verifikasi scan biasanya." He completed a fresh sign-in and the gate did not move. Both sign-in-based theories (v1.9.68's re-login ceremony, the Google-forum token rule behind v1.9.71) are falsified for these accounts by direct experiment: fresh grants still read VALIDATION_REQUIRED on Google's FULL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK and on generate.
- **What verifies, per the owner:** the scan step inside Google's verification flow — the QR code scanned with the phone that is signed into the account. That is the act that lifts the gate in the real client.

The flagged row offers only the account's own verification URL ("verifikasi"); the error panel shows the single "Buka Verifikasi" action plus one muted line stating the scan fact (open the page on another screen, scan its QR with the phone signed into this account). No sign-in action anywhere in the verification UI — settled; do not reintroduce one.
- **Kept:** the generate-oracle recheck (v1.9.63/64) and the v1.9.68 exchange-side reactivation (invisible; only affects a normal re-add).
- **Verification:** build + svelte-check gates at release; staging /api/version read-back after deploy.

## [v1.9.71] - 2026-11-09

## Antigravity verification: bundled verify flow, exactly like agy (v1.9.71)

- **Owner's directive (2026-11-09):** "Kenapa gak sekalian sign ulang kaya agy? Kan AxonRouter juga pake agy?" — the gateway's antigravity provider mirrors agy's client, so its verification must behave like agy's too: one bundled flow, not a bare link.
- **Evidence (Google staff, official Antigravity forum):** after the browser verification completes, "retaining an existing token without signing in again will continue returning VALIDATION_REQUIRED"; the prescribed fix is Verify → wait ~15 min → "Sign in again so a fresh token is issued", and the official app pairs the Verify button with "Sign in again". Measured here all day: browser completions alone never lifted the gate for any of the 4 flagged accounts (FULL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK + generate read-backs), because every gateway grant predates the verifications and same-grant refreshes keep the gated verdict.
- **Change vs v1.9.70:** the flagged row's primary action is again the bundled flow, labelled **Verifikasi** (never "login ulang"): it runs this provider's OAuth sign-in — Google interposes any still-pending verification inside that flow — and the fresh grant lands on the same email-keyed row, which the v1.9.68 exchange reactivates. The error panel pairs the same Verifikasi button with "Buka Halaman Verifikasi" (the raw account URL) so both halves of Google's recipe sit in one place, as in the official app. Quota Tracker's direct verify link is unchanged.
- **Verification:** build + svelte-check gates at release; the positive branch closes when the owner completes one bundled Verifikasi on a flagged account and the FULL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK + generate read-back passes.

## [v1.9.69] - 2026-11-09

## Antigravity verification: sequenced verify flow, matching how it works in the real client (v1.9.69)

- **Symptom:** v1.9.68 framed verification as "re-login" and removed the verification URL from the error panel. The owner corrected this: in Antigravity the gate is lifted by the verification page alone ("verifikasi doang"), not by a login ceremony — and he is right about the page. What the day's evidence proves is WHY the same page never worked from the dashboard.
- **Evidence (2026-11-09, after the owner's browser completions on jayawijayaa116 and anaking966):** `loadCodeAssist` with `mode=FULL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK` — Google's own full eligibility verdict, all modes — still returns free-tier in `ineligibleTiers` with reasonCode `VALIDATION_REQUIRED` for both accounts, and generate still refuses 403. The browser completions never registered at all. His own symptom names the reason: the first click answers "anda tidak login" (you are not signed in) — the verification page binds to the browser session that is signed in as that account, which is exactly the context Antigravity provides (the user is signed in there) and a bare dashboard click does not. The retry shows a success page for an unbound flow and changes nothing server-side.
- **Fix:** the verification action is sequenced, mirroring the real client's context. Row button renamed "verifikasi" (step 1: this provider's OAuth sign-in for the account; the v1.9.68 exchange-side reactivation still applies). The error panel now offers both steps explicitly — "1. Login Ulang" and "2. Buka Verifikasi" (the stored fresh URL, new tab) — with one line of copy explaining the session binding, so both steps happen in one sitting in the same browser.
- **Deliberate divergence:** the JS router still presents the bare verification URL alone (the flow proven not to register); recorded here per repo rule.
- **Verification:** pending the owner's one sequenced pass on a flagged account; server-side read-back (FULL_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK + pinned generate) will confirm whether the flag lifts. Build + svelte-check gates at release.

## [v1.9.68] - 2026-11-09

### Verification is a re-login: flagged Antigravity accounts reactivate through the OAuth sign-in, not the bare error URL

- Mechanism, established live (2026-11-09): VALIDATION_REQUIRED is
  Google's first-use gate — loadCodeAssist lists the free tier under
  `ineligibleTiers` with reasonCode VALIDATION_REQUIRED for accounts
  that have never used Antigravity. The gate lifts account-wide when
  the account completes a real sign-in with the Antigravity client
  (what agy's login does), and ONLY then: the `validation_url` minted
  into API errors — and even the one in loadCodeAssist's
  ineligibleTiers — opened bare in a browser errors (owner saw a 500)
  or "succeeds" without registering anything; all four flagged
  staging accounts stayed generate-gated after repeated browser
  completions, with fresh post-verification tokens, on every surface
  combination probed (with/without project, daily/prod hosts).
- Backend (`oauth/antigravity.go`): the exchange already keyed the
  connection by the sign-in email, so a re-login lands on the same
  row and rebuilds its blob (validation fields drop out). It now
  also detects that the replaced blob was validation-flagged and
  reactivates the connection (`isActive = 1`) in the same UPDATE,
  reporting `reactivated: true` in the response. Manual and ToS
  disables are deliberately NOT reactivated by a re-login. If Google
  still refuses the account after the sign-in, the serving-path
  classifiers re-flag it on the next refusal, so the state stays
  honest.
- Dashboard: the flagged row's primary action on the provider page
  is now **re-login** (runs the provider's OAuth connect modal —
  Google's verification rides inside that sign-in, exactly like
  agy), next to the existing generate-oracle Recheck. The error
  detail panel's "Buka Link Verifikasi Manual" became "Login Ulang
  untuk Verifikasi" doing the same. Quota Tracker no longer sends
  operators to the dead bare link; its two callouts now say the
  account needs a re-login on its provider page (the tracker keeps
  its generate-based Check button). Deliberate divergence from the
  JS reference, which still links the raw validation_url: that path
  is proven not to register, so Go does not offer it as the action.

## [v1.9.67] - 2026-11-09

### Connect modal: step rows stop overflowing on phones, buttons slim to 32px, one-tap Paste for the code

- Owner's phone report (photo of the Connect Antigravity modal):
  Step 1's single row — URL field, Open login page, Copy — does not
  fit a phone: the Copy button was pushed past the modal's edge and
  the Open button's label wrapped into a three-line stack, ballooning
  its height. Step 1 now stacks on small screens: the URL field takes
  its own full-width row (min-w-0 so it can actually shrink), and the
  two actions share an equal-halves row below it; on sm+ the wrapper
  dissolves (sm:contents) and the three sit on one row again. All
  labels are whitespace-nowrap.
- Button heights in the modal are fixed h-8 (32px) instead of
  padding-sized: Step 1's Open/Copy, the new Paste button, Connect /
  Cancel in the footer, and the Kiro social row's Open (whose URL
  field gets the same min-w-0 treatment). The modal shell also trades
  p-6 for p-4 on phones (sm:p-6), returning width to the content.
- Step 2 gains a Paste button beside the code field: one tap reads
  the clipboard (navigator.clipboard.readText) and fills the field,
  trimmed. Clipboard reads need a secure context and permission, so
  an empty clipboard or a refused read leaves a one-line hint under
  the field instead of failing silently — the manual long-press
  paste keeps working everywhere.
- The Step 1 / Step 2 block is shared by every OAuth connect flow
  (Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cline, Freebuff, Kiro social), so
  the redesign lands for all of them at once.

## [v1.9.66] - 2026-11-09

### MiniMax credits: the progress bar returns — rendered the JS way, from the row's own numbers

- Fragment 1050 reverted the backend to the JS shape but also
  dropped the row's progress bar entirely, overshooting the owner's
  order. Reading the actual JS table
  (AxonRouter's ProviderLimits/QuotaTable.js) settles it: the JS
  renderer has NO credit-balance special case — every row draws its
  bar and percentage from its own reported used/total (the pattern
  CodeBuddy's packs make meaningful), and for the MiniMax Credits
  row `{used: 0, total: <balance>}` that is a full bar at 100%
  remaining. The bar suppression for credit rows was a deviation of
  this Go port, not JS behaviour.
- QuotaTable therefore renders bar + percentage for MiniMax credit
  rows again (the `isMiniMaxCredit` carve-outs), now on the JS data
  basis: the v1.9.65 backend row (used 0, total = live balance, no
  synthesized denominator of any kind — no peak, no fixed grant).
  Other providers' credit rows (deepseek, ollama) keep the port's
  amount-only rendering; fragment 1050's removal of the "N/A" reset
  placeholder for credit rows also stands (the owner asked what it
  was for; a balance has no reset time).

## [v1.9.65] - 2026-11-09

### MiniMax credits: back to the JS shape — balance only, no invented percentage, no N/A

- Fragment 1047's peak-relative percentage for the MiniMax Credits
  row invented a denominator (the highest balance ever read) that
  MiniMax never reports: balances differ per account and per top-up,
  so the bar sat at ~100% and drained by hundredths of a percent —
  a progress display with no information. The owner ordered the
  AxonRouter JS / CodeBuddy pattern instead: progress bars are drawn
  only from provider-reported used/total (CodeBuddy's credit packs,
  MiniMax's own M Plan windows), never from a synthesized total.
- Backend: `applyMiniMaxCreditsPeak` and its two call sites are
  removed. The Credits row returns to the exact upstream shape
  (open-sse/services/minimaxCodeUsage.js): `{used: 0, total:
  <balance>, isCreditBalance: true, currency: "credits"}` — a bare
  balance, no remainingPercentage. (Connection blobs written by
  v1.9.62–v1.9.64 keep an inert `creditsPeak` field; nothing reads
  it anymore.) M Plan window rows are untouched: their percentages
  are provider-reported and keep their bars.
- Frontend (QuotaTable): the `isMiniMaxCredit` carve-outs that drew
  a bar and a percentage for the MiniMax credit row are removed, so
  every credit-balance row renders as an amount again. Credit rows
  also no longer render "N/A" in the reset slot (mobile name row and
  desktop reset column): a balance has no reset time, and the JS
  table leaves the cell empty rather than inventing a placeholder.

## [v1.9.64] - 2026-11-09

### Verification-required recheck: wire the chat handler into the production dashboard route table

- Fragment 1048's generate-backed recheck shipped in v1.9.63 but
  could never run in production: `recheckValidationFlag` refuses to
  guess when the dashboard handler has no chat handler, and the
  production dashboard table never had one. `SetupRoutes` wired
  `dashH.Chat` for its own table, but the server router mounts the
  dashboard API through `SetupDashboardRoutes`, which wired
  SemanticCache, Limiter and Resilience from the chat handler and
  left Chat nil — so every quota-read recheck exited at the guard,
  flagged accounts stayed parked with their pre-fix verdicts, and
  the connection test's generate verdict silently fell back to the
  stored message. Proven on staging v1.9.63: usage reads on flagged
  accounts returned in ~2 ms with the stored lastError timestamps
  untouched (no recheck writes at all), while the code was present
  and the version read 1.9.63.
- `SetupDashboardRoutes` now wires `dashH.Chat = chatH` alongside the
  other shared instances. This also gives the production playground
  routes the chat handler their dispatch expects.
- The recheck's re-park also keeps the freshest verification URL:
  when the ping's error body yields no URL, it re-reads the stored
  one before falling back, because the ping's own chat-lane
  classifier may have just stored a newer token from the same
  refusal than the one the recheck started with.

## [v1.9.63] - 2026-11-09

### Verification-required accounts: release verdict moves to a real generate; Verify link stores the account's real flow

- Fragment 1046's auto-recheck released flagged accounts on the light
  account probe (loadCodeAssist). Live evidence 2026-11-09 proved the
  surfaces disagree: for jayawijayaa116@gmail.com the probe answered
  valid while a real `streamGenerateContent` call with the account's
  own refreshed token returned 403 PERMISSION_DENIED /
  VALIDATION_REQUIRED, and the quota surface agreed with generate.
  The probe-based release therefore oscillated — release on the probe,
  re-park on the next quota read — and the operator's Refresh in the
  Quota Tracker could never actually enable an account.
- New `recheckValidationFlag` (dashboard): the release decision for a
  validation-flagged connection is a real generate through the
  ordinary chat lane with the connection pinned (the auto-ping
  machinery; probe-marked, so it never enters the usage ledger, and a
  probe pin is never redirected to another account). The account is
  temporarily reactivated so the pinned lane will serve it; a passing
  generate leaves it released, a failing one re-parks it with the
  freshest verdict. Both release sites use it: the quota-read
  auto-check (fragment 1046's hook) and the connection test itself
  (fragment 973's manual Recheck / the tracker's Check button now
  answer with the generate verdict for flagged Antigravity accounts
  instead of the probe's).
- The Verify link now stores the account-specific verification URL
  the upstream error carries (`error.details[].metadata.validation_url`,
  extracted by a recursive walk of the error payload) at every flag
  writer that sees a fresh error: the generate recheck, and the quota
  surface (`fetchAntigravityDashboardUsage` surfaces it on the usage
  result). The URL's token rotates with each fresh error, so every
  recheck also refreshes the stored link — the operator always opens
  the current flow Google actually gated, not the generic
  `https://antigravity.google` landing page that fragment 1046's code
  stored. The chat-path writers already extracted this URL
  (`extractGoogleValidationURL`); the generic page remains only as a
  fallback when an error carries no URL.
- Non-validation ping failures (transport, timeout) re-park with the
  previously stored verdict instead of overwriting it with noise:
  flagged is the conservative state, and the next read retries the
  check.

## [v1.9.62] - 2026-11-09

### MiniMax credits get a progress bar (peak-relative), like Antigravity's quota rows

- The Quota Tracker drew Antigravity windows as progress bars with a
  percentage but showed a MiniMax account's credits as a bare amount:
  the table deliberately suppresses the bar and the percentage for
  credit-balance rows, and MiniMax reports only a balance — no grant
  total, no consumed amount — so no honest percentage existed.
- The usage read now maintains a per-connection reference on the
  connection blob (`creditsPeak`): the highest balance ever read for
  that connection, raised only by a live read that beats it. The
  Credits row is rewritten against the peak (total = peak,
  used = peak − balance, remaining = balance,
  remainingPercentage = balance / peak × 100), so the share is real:
  it drains as credits are spent and refills when a top-up raises the
  peak.
- The quota table renders the bar and the percentage for MiniMax
  credit rows (other credit-balance providers are untouched), and the
  amount line shows the current balance via the row's `remaining`
  field, falling back to `total` for providers that do not set it.

### Verification-required accounts: automatic recheck on quota reads + a Check button in the Quota Tracker

- Root cause of "I verified the account but it stays disabled": the
  only release path was the manual Recheck on the provider page. The
  quota usage endpoint short-circuits every inactive connection to its
  stored error without any live read, so the Quota Tracker — where the
  operator watches these accounts — could never observe that Google
  accepts the account again, and no automatic check existed.
- `HandleGetConnectionUsage` now special-cases a validation-flagged
  connection (`data.status = validation_required`, the non-terminal
  verdict carved out in fragment 973): the read runs the same probe
  the connection test uses, and `persistProbeResult`'s existing
  verified-transition clears the flag and reactivates the account;
  the read then falls through and serves live quotas. Any other
  verdict keeps returning the stored message. Terminal disables
  (ToS, dead auth) are still never dialed.
- The Quota Tracker row actions gain a Check verification button for
  flagged accounts (the tracker's counterpart of the provider page's
  Recheck): it re-probes via the connection test endpoint and force-
  refreshes the row, so the verdict is visible in place — released
  rows flip straight to their quota table.

## [v1.9.61] - 2026-11-09

### TokenHarbor waves: never report success when no candidate was pickable

- Reviewing the v1.9.60 live-proof logs surfaced a latent hole in the
  new hedged-waves path: if the first wave found zero pickable
  candidates (every connection model-locked at that instant), the wave
  runner returned a nil error, which the caller reads as "request
  served" — the client would get an empty 200 for a request nobody
  attempted. The runner now returns a real 503 upstream error in that
  case, so the caller falls through to the sequential path's standard
  lock/wait handling. With candidates present nothing changes.

## [v1.9.60] - 2026-11-09

### Backfill: docs suite, compose image sourcing, repo prune (ErNor, shipped in this release)

- A standard core documentation suite now lives in `docs/` and is
  linked from the README (commits 976eace5a9, d189730d79).
- The single and cluster compose files now pull the published GHCR
  image instead of building from source; local source builds move to
  the dedicated `docker-compose.build.yml` (commit 2e154b0e).
- Pruned orphaned root screenshots, an empty db artifact, and stale
  discovery notes from the repo (commit ebc5334a).

### TokenHarbor: hedged waves under a 60s admission budget (client-feel tuning)

- Owner directive: for TokenHarbor models the only metric is how fast
  the client feels an answer; backend 429s and spent attempts are free
  collateral because the pool holds ~30K accounts, and there is no
  model substitution. The protections written to spare accounts ran
  against that directive: the sequential path capped TokenHarbor at 2
  account attempts and the executor deliberately never hedged.
- Measured upstream physics (2026-11-09, from hijilaptop): the free
  tier's GPU capacity is one global queue per model whose dominant
  failure shape is silent queueing, not door rejection — a 100-key
  probe answered 14/100 within 45s (success median 19.4s), the rest
  read-timed-out with zero HTTP errors; response headers arrive in a
  ~60s admission tick while first content can lag another ~60s or
  never arrive, so headers are not an admission signal.
- `shouldHedgeProvider` gains a TokenHarbor profile (8 candidates,
  2s stagger, settings overrides still win) and the direct path runs
  `executeHedgedWaves`: waves of fresh candidates until one commits,
  the pool is walked, or the shared admission budget ends the request.
  Fast-failing waves roll immediately into the next wave; identical-
  failure classes (model-fit, unsupported media, model concurrency)
  stop the walk at once.
- Hedged requests for queue-bound providers (any provider with an
  admission budget; today TokenHarbor at 60s) commit on the first body
  bytes, not on response headers, and when the budget dies with no
  winner the gateway cancels everything and returns a 429 that the
  error masker turns into the retryable 503 — so the client retries
  with fresh tickets instead of hanging in silence (the old path once
  left a client without any verdict past 150s). The budget only guards
  the silent admission phase: once a stream flows it is never cut by
  it, however long the generation runs. A manual replica of this
  method measured client TTFT 6.3–34.7s, 3/3 landed, against the
  sequential path's 2/5 in the same conditions.

### Persona owned_by branding, persona snapshot cache, audit cleanups

- `/v1/models` branding (owner order): combo entries now publish
  `owned_by: "AxonRouter"` and Persona virtual models publish
  `owned_by: "Axonrouter_Unrestricted"` (previously `"combo"` and
  `"persona"`). No consumer keyed off the old values.
- Persona definitions are now served from an immutable in-memory
  snapshot on the Repo (mirroring the jailbreak ruleset cache) instead
  of a kv query per lookup: the serving path asks "is this name a
  persona?" on every request and every failover attempt, so the answer
  must not cost a database round trip. Persona writes invalidate the
  snapshot; a failed rebuild degrades to "not a persona" rather than
  failing the request.
- The Persona modal no longer refetches the combo list: the Persona
  page's combos are passed in and shared with the target picker (the
  modal still lazy-loads connections, and combos only if the page's
  fetch came back empty).
- Retired-binding cleanups from the UX/efficiency audit: the global
  excludes copy and the jailbreak comments no longer describe the
  deleted per-model exact bindings as live behaviour, and the unused
  frontend wrapper for the retired binding-catalog endpoint was
  removed (the endpoint itself stays).

## [v1.9.59] - 2026-11-09

# 1041 — Persona becomes virtual models: minted names, picker targets, binding layer retired

## The change of logic (owner's order)
- Setting a persona no longer arms a prompt on a model or combo name
  that already exists. A persona is now a **virtual model**: the
  operator mints a NEW name, picks the target it runs on — a single
  model or a combo, via the Combos model picker — and picks the preset
  it injects from the library (which is unchanged).
- The name must be different from everything else: creation refuses a
  name already used by a catalog model, a combo, a model alias, or
  another persona; combo create/rename refuse a persona's name from
  the other side. A persona may not target another persona, so
  resolution is always one hop.
- Clients call the persona name like any model. `/v1/models` publishes
  it with `owned_by: "persona"`, cloning its target's entry so
  capabilities and limits match what will actually serve.

## Serving path
- `resolveModel` resolves a persona name to its target (model id or
  combo name) before alias/combo handling.
- `applyJailbreak` treats a persona request the way it treats the
  playground override: the persona's own preset replaces the standing
  resolver outright, so no keyword rule stacks underneath it and the
  target's legs cannot re-arm a different preset.

## Retired: per-model exact bindings
- The resolver's exact-binding arm and the explain endpoint's
  exact-binding branch are removed; keyword rules and the exclude
  lists are now the only standing arming mechanisms.
- The binding endpoints (`GET/PUT/DELETE /api/jailbreak/models`) and
  the dashboard binding UI (BindingList, BindModal, BindingBatchBar,
  BulkArm) are deleted; the stored binding rows are wiped from the kv
  store as part of the release. The preset library, its keyword rules,
  excludes, import, preview, and usage counters are untouched.
- The db-layer binding helpers remain as unused surface: the repo's
  existing test files still reference them, and the tests were not
  part of this change (they are reconciled when the suite is next
  maintained).
- The Playground's standing-prompt chip now asks the resolve/explain
  endpoint for the selected model instead of reading the deleted
  binding map; its prompt-decision payload is unchanged.
- Persona page rework: "Persona models" segment with create/edit
  modal (name, picker target, preset combobox); GlobalExcludes moves
  under Presets, alongside the keyword machinery it governs; the
  How-it-works copy is rewritten for the two remaining arming paths.

## Verification
- go build ./... and go vet on the touched packages green;
  svelte-check 0 errors / 0 warnings over 3,904 files; web build
  green.
- Live proofs on staging are recorded with the v1.9.59 release:
  persona listed in /v1/models, prompt-shaped answer through the
  persona name on both a model target and a combo target, collision
  rejections, retired endpoints gone.

## [v1.9.57] - 2026-11-08

# 1036 — Mid-stream transport breaks now penalize the egress pool

## Problem
- When an upstream connection dies AFTER a stream has committed —
  the client already received chunks — the attempt returns the
  body-read error ("http2: response body closed" and kin) instead
  of a status. classifyPoolFailure saw those errors, but
  isProxyTransportError's substring list did not recognize any of
  them, so the pool whose connection snapped took no fitness
  penalty and stayed in rotation. Observed in production shape on
  2026-11-07: 14 stream breaks in ~20 seconds through one ISP pool,
  zero penalty, recovery only when the pool healed on its own.

## Fix
- isProxyTransportError additionally matches "response body closed",
  "stream error", and "connection closed" — the shapes an egress
  leg dying mid-flight produces. Two consecutive failures now bench
  the pool through the existing progressive-cooldown machinery, in
  both the fallback loop and the pinned lane (they share the
  classifier). "context canceled" deliberately stays unmatched: a
  client leaving says nothing about the pool.

## Verification
- A temporary in-package probe exercised the classifier on the new
  shapes plus the negative cases (client cancel, upstream 429) and
  passed; the probe file was removed after the run. go build ./...
  green.

# 1035 — Recent-requests feeds emit the total `tokens` the analytics pulse compares

## Problem
- AnalyticsView's top-request pulse compares RecentRequestItem.tokens,
  but neither recent-requests feed emitted a total: the usage-stats
  feed carried promptTokens/completionTokens only, and the morph feed
  inputTokens/outputTokens only. The comparison was undefined !==
  undefined — the pulse could never fire (found during the fragment
  1032 type cleanup, which documented the field as unemitted).

## Fix
- axonRecentRequest gains `tokens` (prompt + completion), set at its
  single construction site; the morph recent-request map gains the
  same total from its row. The client type comment now states the
  field is emitted by both feeds.
- The sibling `proxy` field stays a documented reservation: no
  history feed carries an egress column, and no recent-requests view
  renders one (the realtime table's proxy comes from the live
  request ledger, a different feed).

## Verification
- go build ./... green; live after deploy: the usage-stats payload's
  recentRequests items carry "tokens" equal to prompt + completion.

## [v1.9.55] - 2026-11-08

# 1033 — Provider stats: remove the SQL aggregate shortcut that bypassed the census

## Symptom (found in v1.9.54 live verification)
- GET /api/providers/stats served `"states":{}` for every provider:
  the per-state census of fragment 1031 never reached the client,
  even though computeProviderSummaryStats filled it.

## Root cause
- HandleProviderStats preferred a "high-performance" SQL GROUP BY
  fast path that built providerSummaryStat literals from
  total/connected/disabled counts only. The full computation ran
  only when the SQL path errored or returned no rows — effectively
  never. The same shortcut had been silently zeroing the error and
  exhausted fields (and lastErrorAt) all along; the strip's legacy
  fast-path derivation masked it while full lists were loaded.

## Fix
- The SQL shortcut is deleted. The handler always computes from the
  connection rows via computeProviderSummaryStats, so every field —
  census included — comes from the one derivation. The cost is
  bounded by the handler's existing 10-minute cache and by the
  Repo's snapshot cache behind GetProviderConnections; the endpoint
  serves the dashboard only.

## Verification
- go build + go vet on the dashboard package.
- Live on staging after deploy: the stats payload carries a states
  census per provider whose counts sum to total, and antigravity's
  census equals an independent per-row derivation over its
  connections (the client's own rules).

# 1031 — Provider summary stats carry the per-health-state census; the strip's paged fast path reads real counts

## Symptom
- On providers whose connection list is paged (fragment 1028), the
  account-status strip took its counts from the summary stats' three
  derivable buckets only: Active, Error, and a Disabled remainder.
  Needs-verification, cooldown and locked accounts read 0 and their
  counts were swept into Disabled — the verification state shipped in
  v1.9.48 was invisible exactly on the large providers.

## Root cause
- providerSummaryStat exposed only total / connected / exhausted /
  error / allDisabled, a coarser classification than the six health
  states the strip renders, so the fast path had nothing truthful to
  read for the other buckets.

## Fix
- internal/handlers/dashboard/batch2_stats.go: providerSummaryStat
  gains `states`, a per-state census counted in the same pass.
  healthStateForConnection mirrors deriveConnectionHealth in
  connectionHealth.ts step for step (verification demand first, then
  disabled, rate_limited -> cooldown, the error family, any live lock
  via the existing activeModelLocks/futureTime parsers, else active),
  reusing providers.EffectiveStatusWithError so the verdict itself is
  never re-derived.
- web: ProviderStats and the summary-stats payload type carry the
  census through getProviderStats (summed across auth types); the
  strip's fast path fills every bucket from it and keeps the old
  three-bucket derivation only for payloads that predate the census.

## Verification
- go build + go vet on the touched packages.
- Live on staging after deploy: summary stats for a paged provider
  carry states whose sum equals total, and the strip's buckets match
  a direct census of the same provider's connections.

# 1026 — Speculative hedging and model-concurrency handling (retroactive record)

> Recorded retroactively at the owner's order: this change shipped inside
> the v1.9.53 feature commit (89ec6915) without its fragment; this file is
> the backfilled record, not a new change.

## What landed
- Provider strategies gain hedge settings (`hedgeEnabled`, `hedgeDelayMs`,
  `hedgeMaxAttempts` in internal/db/settings.go).
- internal/handlers/chat/hedging.go: speculative multi-account racing.
  Candidates are staggered by the hedge delay (default 120 ms, cap 2);
  the first candidate to answer HTTP 200 commits its headers and stream
  to the client through a buffering response writer, and the coordinator
  cancels every loser immediately. Pinned requests never hedge (the
  pinned branch returns first), probe contexts never hedge, and session
  affinity/rotation ordering is applied before candidates are picked.
- Hedging is ON by default for the dahl provider only (hundreds of farm
  accounts, fast-moving GPU-slot saturation); every other provider is
  opt-in via its strategy. The combo path wires the same executor,
  gated on the leg carrying no pinned connection.
- Model-concurrency saturation (providers.IsModelConcurrencyError) is
  now terminal for the account loop: the model is locked on that
  connection for 30 s, a scoped error is recorded, and retries break
  instead of walking the whole farm. Dahl additionally records a
  process-local 30 s cluster block per model (dahl_concurrency.go).
- Dahl accounts answering 402 / quota-exhausted / invalid-key / 401 are
  disabled with a stored reason instead of being retried forever.
- TokenHarbor cooldowns pass through TokenHarborAdjustedCooldown so a
  parsed "next request in ..." window is no longer applied verbatim.

## Verification (at review time)
- Code review of hedging.go, fallback.go and the combo wiring: winner
  commitment is first-bytes only (pre-first-token), losers are
  context-cancelled, pin semantics preserved. Whether a cancelled loser
  that already started generating leaves a billable usage row is NOT
  yet proven — flagged for a live probe.

## [v1.9.52] - 2026-11-08

# 1025 — Playground fits the shell exactly: the chat thread is the only scroller

## Symptom
- After the 1024 redesign the page still scrolled: the console root
  was sized `100dvh - 1.5rem` (main's padding), but the dashboard
  shell renders a TopBar above <main>, so the view overshot the
  available height by the TopBar's height and <main> scrolled anyway.

## Fix
- PlaygroundView measures its real container instead of guessing
  viewport math: on mount it finds the closest <main>, locks its
  overflow (restored on unmount), and sizes the console to main's
  content box (clientHeight minus the 24px padding) under a
  ResizeObserver, so the fit stays exact across window resizes,
  sidebar changes and phone rotation. The chat thread — already the
  only internal overflow-y-auto — becomes the single scroller.

## Verification
- bun run build: OK. svelte-check: no findings in the touched file.
- Live on staging after deploy (see release notes).

  picker trigger, a prompt chip naming the layer that will fire —
  Session prompt / preset name / Standing: <name> / No prompt — a
  parameters chip, Clear), a one-line served-by note, and the thread
  filling the rest. Prompt + parameters moved into a single "Session
  settings" modal; all state, precedence and the send path are
  unchanged.
- ModelPicker is a trigger button + searchable modal: groups (Combos
  first, then providers) filter by model, provider or connection
  name; the selected model stays checked.
- ChatThread: document-style rows instead of chat bubbles — user
  turns in a subtle block, assistant turns in a markdown body rendered
  by a new XSS-safe mini renderer (markdown.ts escapes the model text
  first, then rebuilds code fences, inline code, bold/italic,
  headings, bullet and numbered lists, and blockquotes from its own
  tags only — model output never reaches {@html} raw). All blocks
  wrap inside the chat column: code blocks use pre-wrap and long
  words/URLs break, so nothing overflows the thread sideways. While a reply is pending it shows a pulsing
  "Waiting for the model… Ns" row driven by a live clock in the view,
  then a blinking cursor while tokens stream. Completed replies gain
  a Copy button beside the existing meta line. The empty state offers
  suggestion chips that fill the composer. The composer auto-grows,
  and the thread only auto-scrolls while the reader is near the
  bottom.

## Verification
- bun run build: OK (bundle numbers in the release notes).
- The renderer was executed directly on a sample covering bold,
  inline code, a long-line fenced block, a blockquote, a numbered
  list and a <script> payload: all formatted as intended and the
  payload came out escaped.
- svelte-check (app tsconfig): baseline held for the touched files.

## [v1.9.50] - 2026-11-08

# 1023 — Playground inventory deduped per (provider, model): the picker loads again at farm scale

## Symptom
- The Playground showed "No active connections. Enable a provider
  connection first" while staging held tens of thousands of active
  connections. GET /api/playground/models answered 200 with ~314k
  entries (~59 MB, ~3.5 s server-side): one entry per model PER
  CONNECTION, so a 31k-key provider farm duplicated its small model
  catalog tens of thousands of times and the browser never got a
  loadable list — the picker fell through to its empty state.

## Root cause
- The inventory deliberately attributed each model to every connection
  publishing it (fragment 1008 design, "grouped by provider +
  connection"), which was right at 19 connections and fatal at farm
  scale. The playground chat dispatch never pins a connection — the
  serving path picks the account — so the duplicates carried no
  capability, only payload.

## Fix
- playgroundInventory dedupes entries by (provider, model), keeping
  the first eligible connection as the attribution, and caps
  contributing connections per provider at 100
  (playgroundProviderConnectionCap): real fleets (dozens of accounts
  per provider, where per-account model pins matter) are covered in
  full; farm providers publish their catalog once. Payload drops from
  ~314k entries / ~59 MB to the few hundred distinct models.

## Verification
- go build + vet clean (see release notes for live counts).

## [v1.9.48] - 2026-11-08

# 1021 — Account verification state: visible in the UI, clearable by recheck

## Symptom
- An antigravity account hit by Google's "Verify your account to continue.
  PERMISSION_DENIED VALIDATION_REQUIRED" demand was parked as a generic
  "disabled" row: the stored verification URL never surfaced, nothing
  showed whether the operator had already verified the account upstream,
  and the probe path refused to re-check it at all — persistProbeResult
  and testSingleConnection treat any stored "disabled" verdict as
  terminal (fragment 973), and a validation row carries
  testStatus "disabled", so even after verifying at Google the account
  stayed parked until a manual reset-status.

## Root cause
- The validation state existed only as scattered data keys
  (status "validation_required", verificationUrl, lastError) with no
  health state of its own: the client derivation folded it into
  "disabled", and the probe persister could not distinguish the
  recoverable validation verdict from a terminal ToS disable.

## Fix
- Probe path (internal/handlers/dashboard/connection_probe.go):
  storedDisabledMessage no longer treats status "validation_required"
  as terminal (the status field is the canonical verdict — both disable
  writers set status "disabled"; testStatus alone now only counts for
  legacy rows without a status). persistProbeResult: when a
  validation-flagged connection probes valid, the flag is cleared
  (status/verificationUrl/validationMessage/validationAt deleted) and
  the connection is reactivated via SetConnectionStatus(true) — the
  "verified" transition, proven by the upstream accepting the account.
  A probe that fails again keeps the flag.
- Dashboard: connectionHealth derives a distinct "validation" state
  (verificationUrl present, or a disabled verdict whose lastError
  carries the validation markers) ahead of "disabled"; the account
  status strip gains a "Needs verification" segment; the provider
  detail row shows a "needs verification" badge with a Verify link
  (the stored Google URL, manual click) and a Recheck button that
  re-probes the account and refreshes the row.

## Verification
- go build ./... and go vet on the dashboard handler: clean.
- bun run build: OK (dist 5.3 MB). svelte-check (app tsconfig):
  89 errors / 56 warnings, equal to the pristine-HEAD baseline.
- Live on staging after deploy (see release notes).

## [v1.9.46] - 2026-11-08

# 1019 — Apply Proxy binds the provider once; per-account marks are custom-only

## Symptom

- The provider page's Apply Proxy modal applied a uniform choice (a
  proxy group, a proxy type, one pool, or None) by writing that value
  into EVERY connection of the provider, one sequential update request
  per connection. On tokenharbor (31,456 connections) the operator
  watched it grind through rows one by one; a partial run left 2,231
  connections stamped `group:cloudflare` before it was abandoned.

## Root cause

- The modal was an upstream port whose bulk apply ignored the
  provider-level binding this gateway already has: the provider
  strategy (`providerStrategies[<provider>]`), which accounts inherit
  dynamically per request via `applyProviderProxyPool`. Stamping every
  account duplicated that default 31k times — and worse, an explicit
  per-account binding outranks the provider lock, so every stamped
  account was frozen to that day's choice, immune to later
  provider-level changes.

## Fix

- `handleApplyProxyPool` in ProviderDetailView now routes uniform
  choices to the provider strategy as ONE settings write: a group or
  type goes through the existing Proxy Lock write
  (`applyProxyGroupLock`); a single pool goes through the new
  `applyProviderProxyPool`, which stores the bare pool id in the
  strategy's `proxyPoolId` (the resolver returns it verbatim and the
  serving path resolves that one pool) with no `proxyGroup` mirror;
  None clears the provider binding. Accounts without a custom mark go
  direct; custom per-account marks are untouched and keep winning.
- Only the one-to-one rotation still stamps per connection —
  distributing accounts across pools is a per-account marking by
  definition — and the modal copy says so.
- The lock state, label and row badges learned the pool form of the
  binding: a bare strategy `proxyPoolId` surfaces as
  `lockedProxyPoolId` ("Pool <name>" in the lock label, "Pool: <name>
  (auto)" in `proxyBadgeInfo` inherit badges) instead of being read as
  a group selector or shown as no binding.
- Deliberate divergence from upstream behaviour, recorded per repo
  rules: upstream stamps all connections; this gateway binds the
  provider once.
- Data cleanup on staging (not code): the 2,231 partial-run
  `group:cloudflare` stamps on tokenharbor connections were removed;
  they duplicated the provider's existing cloudflare binding, so
  routing is unchanged and those accounts inherit again.

## [v1.9.45] - 2026-11-08

# 1018 — Pinned-connection failures now penalize proxy pool fitness

## Symptom

- A stalling egress pool (ISP-BD-SG-06) hung two antigravity requests for
  the full 30s probe timeout on 2026-11-08 (~03:39–03:40 WIB) and stayed
  in rotation with a healthy-looking fitness score (71.9, no cooldown, no
  recorded failures). The operator had to bench it by hand.

## Root cause

- Pool fitness penalties (smart.FitnessTracker.RecordFailure /
  RecordFailureWithCooldown) were recorded only inside the
  multi-connection fallback loop in `handleAccountFallback` (and the
  combo loop). A request with a pinned connection — the idle prober pins
  every connection it checks (`PingConnection`), as does any client
  sending `x-connection-id` — takes the pinned shortcut straight to
  `tryForwardWithConnection` and never enters that loop, so its failures
  were never classified against the pool that served them. Successes on
  the same lane did reach the tracker (recorded inside
  `tryForwardWithConnection`), so a pool could look purely successful
  while hanging pinned attempts indefinitely.
- The two hung attempts were idle-probe pings (body "hi", model
  gemini-3.8-flash-low, ~29.9s each = the probe's 30s PingTimeout). The
  gateway log for the window shows fitness penalties for other providers'
  pools but none for the probe's pool, confirming the bypass.

## Fix

- New `internal/handlers/chat/pool_fitness.go`: `classifyPoolFailure`
  holds the loop's existing classification verbatim (location refusal →
  24h lock via RecordFailureWithCooldown + poolstate.MarkUnfit; transport
  failure → RecordFailure with progressive cooldown), resolving the
  serving pool via the shared `attemptPoolID` (ResolvedProxyPoolID, then
  the connection's configured pool; "__none__"/"direct" excluded).
- The fallback loop now calls `classifyPoolFailure` and keeps its
  exclude-and-retry behaviour on the returned pool.
- The pinned branch of `handleAccountFallback` classifies a failed
  attempt through the same helper before returning the error. No retry
  is added — pinned means pinned — but the pool verdict is now recorded,
  so two consecutive stalls on any lane bench the pool automatically
  (30s cooldown, then 2m + unfit mark at the second consecutive failure).
- ISP-BD-SG-06 itself was benched manually on staging (isActive=false)
  ahead of this fix; the fix is what makes the next stalling pool bench
  itself.

## [v1.9.44] - 2026-11-08

# 1017 — Usage Overview topology nodes keep their positions

## Symptom

On /dashboard/usage, provider nodes on the topology map changed position
constantly: a provider arriving, going quiet, or merely moving in the
activity order reshuffled every node on the ring, so the map could not be
read at a glance and the operator's pan jumped on every membership change.

## Root cause

`ProviderTopologyCard.svelte` placed nodes purely by list position: the
angle was `-π/2 + 2π·idx/s` with `s = providers.length`, and the ring
radii were functions of the same `s` (`rx = max(320, 204·s/2π)`,
`ry = max(200, 0.55·rx)`). The `providers` prop is activity-ordered, so
any membership or order change altered every angle and the ring size at
once. The view layer compounded it: the card refit (resetting pan) on
every node-count change.

## Fix

- New pure module `web/src/components/analytics/topologyLayout.ts`: a
  session slot allocator plus ring geometry. Each provider owns a
  numbered slot keyed by its id (the same lowercased identity the card
  already matches activity against):
  - a present provider keeps its slot unconditionally;
  - a provider that leaves frees its slot for newcomers, but the slot is
    remembered — on return it reclaims the same seat while it is free
    (a slot another present provider owns is never taken back);
  - a newcomer takes the lowest free slot;
  - ring capacity comes from a coarse tier ladder (6/12/18/24/36/48/64)
    covering the highest slot in use, and never shrinks during the
    session, so radii and angles are stable; a tier step forced by a
    genuinely larger concurrent set is the only moment existing angles
    may change.
  Angle and radii derive from slot and capacity only, using the card's
  existing formulas with capacity in place of the live count.
- `ProviderTopologyCard.svelte` consumes the allocator: placement is
  keyed by provider id, the prop order no longer affects it, and the
  refit effect now fires only when the ring size itself changes (a tier
  step), so arrivals and departures no longer reset the operator's pan.
  Hub, edges, artwork, active/pulse/last/error highlighting, drag/pan,
  zoom controls, and the empty state are unchanged.
- `AnalyticsView.svelte` is untouched: its derivation decides who is on
  the map (the 10-minute retention of fragment 1016), the card now
  decides where they sit.
- Known boundary: slot memory lives in the card's component state, so
  it lasts while the card stays mounted; leaving the Usage view and
  coming back starts a fresh assignment (in the same first-seen order
  the old layout used).

## Verification

- Web build via the heavy gate: green.
- svelte-check (`--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`): baseline
  89 errors / 56 warnings, unchanged.
- Allocator exercised directly (scratch script, since removed) against
  the shipped module: A, B, C placed at capacity 6 → B leaves, A and C
  coordinates bit-identical → B returns, reclaims its slot exactly →
  newcomer D takes B's freed slot while A and C stay put → list reorder
  moves nobody → a 7th concurrent provider steps capacity to 12 (the
  one allowed movement) and later departures never shrink it, survivors
  keeping their post-growth seats.

# 1016 — Usage Overview topology retention is 10 minutes, end to end

## Symptom

On /dashboard/usage, a provider dropped off the topology map after five
quiet minutes. The owner raised the retention to a full 10 minutes
(2026-11-08), superseding his 2026-11-04 five-minute rule.

## Root cause

Two layers clipped presence at or below the old window:

- Frontend: `TOPOLOGY_RETENTION_MS` in
  `web/src/components/analytics/AnalyticsView.svelte` was `5 * 60_000`,
  and the presence derivation (`topologyProviders`) gates every source on
  it.
- Backend: the derivation's durable source is
  `stats.byProvider[key].lastUsed` from `GET /api/usage/stats`, but whole
  period families could not supply it. Daily windows (7d/30d/60d/all)
  aggregate `usageDaily` rows, which are keyed by date and carry no time
  of day, so their `byProvider` entries always had an empty `lastUsed`;
  the "today" window starts at midnight. On a freshly loaded page with a
  daily period selected, a provider whose last request was 6–9 minutes
  old therefore had no `lastUsed` at all and survived only if it happened
  to sit in the recent-requests backstop (the latest 60 raw rows).

## Fix

- `AnalyticsView.svelte`: `TOPOLOGY_RETENTION_MS` is now `10 * 60_000`;
  the presence-rule comments state the 10-minute rule dated 2026-11-08
  superseding the 2026-11-04 five-minute rule.
- `internal/handlers/usage_stats.go` (`HandleUsageStats`): after the
  period window is aggregated and before totals are summed, overlay each
  `byProvider` entry's `LastUsed` with the provider's newest raw
  `usageHistory` timestamp inside the retention window
  (`Repo.GetUsageGroupByProviderSince(now − 10m)`, answered by the
  `idx_uh_ts_prov` index). The overlay only raises entries the selected
  window already aggregated — it never creates one — so period totals
  and breakdown membership are unchanged; a provider quiet for longer
  than 10 minutes keeps its previous (possibly empty) `lastUsed` and
  expires from the map on the normal rule. Side effect, intended: in a
  daily period, the provider breakdown's Last Used cell now shows a real
  timestamp for a provider active within the last 10 minutes instead of
  staying blank; providers quiet longer stay blank there, as before.

## Verification

- Web build via the heavy gate: green.
- `go build ./...` via the heavy gate: green.
- svelte-check (`--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`): baseline
  89 errors / 56 warnings, unchanged.
- Fresh-load case traced end to end: for the default "today" and "24h"
  periods the raw window cache already fills `lastUsed` with the newest
  in-window request; for daily periods the new overlay supplies it for
  any provider active within the retention window; the recent-requests
  stamps remain as a backstop in both paths.
- Existing test expectations re-checked by reading (suite not run, per
  the standing rule): `TestHandleUsageStats_DailyByProviderHasNoLastUsed`
  (sqlite_legacy-quarantined) seeds no `usageHistory` rows, so the
  overlay is a no-op for its fixture and its expectation still holds; no
  web test asserts the retention window.
- Other 5-minute constants in the tree (combo failover grace, account
  pacing cap, latency window default, analytics chart labels) are
  different rules and are untouched.

## [v1.9.42] - 2026-11-08

# 1014 — Provider detail page shows account/API-key health (error, cooldown, locked, disabled)

## Symptom

- On a provider detail page (e.g. /dashboard/providers/tokenharbor) there was
  no way to see at a glance which of the provider's accounts/API keys were in
  error, in cooldown, locked, or disabled. The rows showed a probe-driven
  badge (testStatus + a live one-by-one probe), and the server-computed
  `effectiveStatus` was not consumed by the frontend at all.
- `GET /api/connections` could emit `effectiveStatus: "<nil>"` with
  `isEffectivelyActive: false` for healthy, active API keys.

## Root cause

- `sanitizeProviderConnection` (internal/handlers/dashboard/connections.go)
  computed the status with `fmt.Sprintf("%v", safe["testStatus"])`. The
  sanitized map only carries `testStatus` when the stored blob recorded a
  verdict (or the fatal-disable path forced one), so for never-probed
  connections the key was absent and `%v` of a nil interface produced the
  literal string `"<nil>"`, which the status engine then returned verbatim
  as the effective status. Connections with an empty/unreadable data blob
  also returned early with no status fields at all.
- The detail view derived its row badges purely from `testStatus` + the
  one-by-one probe state, so server verdicts (quota_exhausted,
  rate_limited, unavailable, expired — including ones derived from
  lastError classification) never surfaced, and live model locks showed
  only as a ⏱ countdown with no model name or expiry.

## Fix

- Backend (connections.go): the test status is now read as a string
  (`safe["testStatus"].(string)` semantics — a missing verdict reaches the
  status engine as `""`, the never-probed case) via a shared
  `decorateEffectiveStatus` helper, and the decoration now runs on every
  return path of `sanitizeProviderConnection`, including the empty/invalid
  data early returns.
- Frontend:
  - `client.ts`: `ProviderConnection` gains the server status fields
    (effectiveStatus, isEffectivelyActive, statusVariant, disabledReason,
    disabledAt, rateLimitedUntil, backoffLevel), plus a
    `getModelAvailability()` wrapper for the locks census
    (GET /api/models/availability) with its `ModelAvailabilityEntry` type.
  - New `connectionHealth.ts`: one health state per connection
    (active / error / cooldown / locked / disabled) derived from the
    server `effectiveStatus` with the precedence of
    internal/providers/connection_status.go (disabled toggle first, then
    the throttle verdict, then the error family), with live locks merged
    from the census rows and the connection payload's own `modelLock_*`
    keys (the census SQL prefilter keys on the `modelLocks` object shape,
    so flattened-only locks are supplemented from the payload — the same
    source the row's ⏱ timer already reads).
  - New `ProviderAccountStatusStrip.svelte`: a counts strip
    (Active / Error / Cooldown / Locked / Disabled, with the affected
    account names in each chip's tooltip) rendered above the provider's
    connections list, in the rows' existing badge vocabulary.
  - ProviderDetailView wiring only: fetches the census on the same cycle
    the connections refresh (provider open + parent reloads, no new
    polling), renders the strip, and adds row badges — a lock badge
    naming the locked model (+N more) with remaining time and full
    model/until list in the tooltip (the bare ⏱ lock timer yields to
    it), a cooldown pill for a rate_limited verdict with no recorded
    reset, and the server error verdict when the probe badge called the
    connection "active". The disabled badge gains a "· ToS" qualifier
    when the payload marks an upstream terms-of-service disable.
  - Refresh/liveness: the counts and badges re-derive on the view's
    existing 1s clock, so a lock that lapses while the page is open drops
    out without a refetch.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the dashboard handler package via the
  heavy gate: green.
- Web build via the heavy gate: green.
- svelte-check (`--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`): 89 errors / 56 warnings,
  exactly the pre-existing baseline.
- Direct check of the fixed decoration logic: an active connection whose
  stored blob has no `testStatus` now resolves through the
  never-probed branch of EffectiveStatusWithError ("" input) instead of
  returning `"<nil>"`; disabled and fatal-disable paths still force
  `testStatus: "disabled"` before decoration, so their verdicts are
  unchanged.

## [v1.9.42] - 2026-11-08

# 1014 — TokenHarbor custom executor & precision 429 classification

## Symptom

TokenHarbor upstream requests were handled via plain OpenAI forward without custom error classification. Rate limit messages ("Rate limit reached. You can send your next request in 59 min 1 s.") and model capacity limits were treated identically, and proxy egress IP limits ("sharing this network address") risked unnecessary account locks.

## Fix

- Custom `ForwardTokenHarbor` executor ensuring SSE `stream_options: { include_usage: true }`.
- Zero speculative hedging to prevent concurrency quota exhaustion on slow upstream free queues.
- Precision 429 classification in `classifyTokenHarbor`:
  - Model capacity limits (`"model is at capacity"`) trigger short model-scoped locks.
  - Hourly key throttles (`"You can send your next request in X min Y s"`) dynamically parse exact retry durations and park only the affected account.
  - Shared egress IP limits (`"many free accounts are sharing this network address"`) rotate the proxy pool without penalizing account status.

## [v1.9.41] - 2026-11-08

# 1013 — Persona presets gain a third injection position: replace

## Symptom

A Persona preset could only add its prompt around the client's own system
prompt — prepended before it or appended after it. There was no way to make
the persona prompt the *only* system content: a client that ships its own
strong system prompt kept it in force next to the persona's, and the two
could fight. The owner asked for the missing third option ("gak ada sistem
replace?") after comparing prepend and append in the preset editor.

## Root cause

`injectSystemPrompt` (`internal/handlers/chat/jailbreak.go`) normalized
every position other than `"append"` to `"prepend"`, so a stored
`"replace"` could never reach the injection logic — and the preset
editor's form loader coerced anything that was not `"append"` back to
`"prepend"` as well.

## Fix

- `injectSystemPrompt` accepts `"replace"` as a distinct position
  (normalization unchanged otherwise: only exact `"append"`/`"replace"`
  are special, everything else still falls back to `"prepend"`). For
  replace, the client's own system content is discarded per wire shape:
  - Claude top-level `system`: a string becomes the persona prompt alone;
    a block array becomes a single-element array holding the persona block.
  - Gemini `system_instruction`: `parts` becomes a single-element array
    holding the persona part.
  - OpenAI `messages`: every system/developer message is removed and the
    persona system message is inserted at the index of the first removed
    one (index 0 when there were none), so the remaining messages keep
    their relative order.
  The existing idempotency guard (prompt already present in a system slot
  → no-op) runs before the replace branch in every shape, exactly as it
  does for prepend/append. A body with no `messages` at all already fell
  back to a lone persona system message, which is replace by construction.
  Prepend/append behaviour, `prependSystemPrompt`, and turns mode
  (`injectChatTurns`) are untouched.
- No other Go site needed extending: the preset save handler passes the
  doc through without validating position, the DB stores the doc
  generically as JSON (position only defaults to `"prepend"` when empty —
  its field comment now names all three values), and the playground passes
  a chosen preset's stored doc through verbatim (its ad-hoc session prompt
  stays hardcoded to prepend by design).
- Web: the position radio group in `PromptField.svelte` gains
  "Replace (discard the client's system prompt)"; the `JailbreakDoc`
  position type in `client.ts` and the `PresetFormState` type in
  `types.ts` widen to `'prepend' | 'append' | 'replace'`, and
  `presetToForm` no longer coerces a stored `replace` back to `prepend`;
  `PresetCard.svelte` renders a red "Replace" chip next to the existing
  blue "Append" and neutral "Prepend" chips.
- Noted, deliberately unchanged: the dashboard payload preview
  (`HandlePreviewJailbreak`) builds its sample messages with a hardcoded
  prepend for every preset — it never simulated append either. Making it
  faithful means routing the preview through the chat package's

## Verification

Fragment 1011 gave the Persona binding editor a target picker, but it was a
persona-local native `<select>` — a second, poorer picker next to the one

same UI, reused, not a parallel implementation ("pick model ui nya kaya di

## [v1.9.38] - 2026-11-08

# Persona page UI redesign — segmented workspaces, preset cards, Markdown prompt editor (1009)

## Symptom

The Persona page (tab id `jailbreak`) was a single ~2,265-line component
rendering every workspace as one endless scroll: the preset library, the
preset editor, keyword rules, chat-turn scripts, the per-model bindings,
bulk arming, test-match, and the global exclude list all stacked on one
page. Presets rendered as dense table rows with no prompt preview, the
page carried three summary cards plus two full list cards before the
operator reached the control they came for, and nothing about the layout
distinguished the two distinct jobs the page does — writing prompts and
arming them.

## Root cause

The page grew feature by feature (#1–#8 additions: import, bulk arm,
test-match, payload preview, usage counters, batch selection…) and each
one appended its state, handlers, and markup to the same file, so the
structure never caught up with the feature set.

## Fix

UI/UX only — no backend or API changes; every call, payload, and
validation is byte-identical to before.

- **Split** `web/src/components/JailbreakView.svelte` (2,265 lines) into a
  252-line composing view plus `web/src/components/persona/`: `PresetGrid`,
  `PresetCard`, `PresetEditor`, `PromptField`, `TurnEditor`,
  `PresetImport`, `BindingList`, `BindingBatchBar`, `BindModal`,
  `BulkArm`, `TestMatchModal`, `GlobalExcludes`, and `types.ts` (form
  state). `KeywordRules` and `Pagination` are reused as-is.
- **Structure**: in-page segmented tabs **[Presets | Bindings]** replace
  the stacked scroll. A slim header strip carries the page title, a
  one-line description, and the live counts (presets, bindings armed,
  injections); the active segment's primary action (New Preset / Add
  Binding, plus Test match) sits in the segment bar. The global exclude
  list lives under Bindings, which it governs; the "How it works"
  reference stays collapsed at the bottom.
- **Presets segment**: presets are cards in a responsive grid (1 column
  on the phone, 2–3 on wide screens) — name, a 2–3 line monospace prompt
  excerpt, chips for kind, mode (Single/Chat), position (Prepend/Append),
  Gemini safety state, hit count, and Edit/Duplicate/Delete. Filter,
  sort, page size, batch select/export/delete, and pagination are
  unchanged; an empty library now gets a proper empty state with a
  New Preset call to action.
- **Bindings segment**: compact rows — a labelled grid (Target / Preset /
  Inject) on wide screens, stacked cards on the phone. Each row shows a
  MODEL/COMBO type chip (combo names come from the existing combos API),
  the bound preset name, the enable Toggle, and Edit/Unbind. Batch
  rebind/enable/disable/unbind, filters, and pagination are unchanged;
  the add/edit binding modal (Single free-text id + Bulk catalog arm)
  keeps every behaviour, including the keyword-coverage hint.
- **Editor**: still modal-first. The Write form is organised into
  labelled sections — **Prompt** (id, name, injection mode, position,

  (include rules, excludes). The prompt field is now a **Markdown
  editor**: a helper line shows the Markdown structure, and the existing
  rendered Preview (via `marked`) sits beside it; the prompt is stored
  and injected verbatim as Markdown, exactly as before. Chat-mode turn
  editor, file/URL import tabs with their log, and the test-match modal
  with payload preview all survive in their own components.
