## [v1.9.37] - 2026-11-08

# Playground chat — active-connection models, Persona prompt injection (1008)

## Symptom

The dashboard had no way to chat with a model through the gateway itself.
Testing a connection, a combo, or a Persona preset meant pointing an
external client at /v1 with a real API key, and the only model lists
available were catalogs — /v1/models publishes providers, not the
per-connection inventory an operator actually wants to pick from, and
nothing let the operator try a one-off system prompt or a preset against
a model without first binding it as that model's standing configuration.

## Root cause

No playground surface existed: no endpoint aggregated "models on active
connections right now", no dashboard caller identity existed for usage
attribution (the ledger names its caller from the authenticated API key,
which a browser session does not have), and the Persona injector
(applyJailbreak) resolved its document only from the standing per-model
configuration, so a session-scoped prompt decision had nowhere to ride.

## Fix

- **Model inventory** — `GET /api/playground/models` (dashboard session
  group) returns combos first, then one entry per model for every usable
  connection: `{type: 'model'|'combo', provider, connectionId?,
  connectionName?, model}` with `model` the wire id a client would send.
  Usable mirrors the serving path's model-independent eligibility
  (pinnedConnectionIneligible's pre-model checks): `isActive`, and not
  inside an account cooldown park (`db.ConnectionBlockedUntil`;
  ToS-disabled accounts are excluded via `isActive`, which
  DisableConnectionWithReason flips off). Hidden providers are not
  offered, as in /v1/models. Each connection's model set is computed by
  `appendConnectionModels` — the same per-connection builder /v1/models
  uses — with a fresh seen-set per connection, so every connection is
  attributed its own full list.
- **Chat** — `POST /api/playground/chat` translates the playground body
  into an ordinary OpenAI chat body and dispatches it through
  `HandleChatCompletions` itself on a clone of the caller's request: the
  same proxy binding, guardrails, stall gate and usage logging as client
  traffic, SSE streamed chunk-for-chunk, and client abort cancelling the
  same context. Caller identity is a real apiKeys row named exactly
  **playground** (loaded or minted once, cached on the handler, no
  allowlist = unrestricted like any pre-policy key), placed on the
  context under the same slot the auth middleware fills, so usage rows
  and request details name the caller "playground". The handler echoes
  the request's `req_<hex>` id in an `X-Request-ID` response header
  (operator surface only; /v1 keeps not echoing it).
- **Prompt precedence** — the request's prompt decision rides the context
  as a `playgroundPromptOverride` that `applyJailbreak` honors before the
  standing resolver: a non-empty `systemPrompt` injects as a single-mode
  prepend doc; else `presetId` loads that Persona preset from the
  existing store and injects it; else `applyStandingPersona: false`
  suppresses the standing configuration. Any override present means the
  standing resolver is never consulted, so the sources can never stack.
  Injection itself is the extracted `applyJailbreakDoc` — the one
  injector, shared by the standing path and the playground (per-format
  placement via the existing machinery, usage counter, Gemini safety
  flag). Routes are registered in both route tables
  (SetupDashboardRoutes and dashboard.RegisterRoutes, the latter via a
  new `DashboardHandler.Chat` wired in SetupRoutes).
- **Frontend** — new `playground` tab (nav main group, route
  `/dashboard/playground`, PAGE_META) with components under
  `web/src/components/playground/`: PlaygroundView (composition + send /
  stream orchestration), ModelPicker (grouped by provider — connection,
  combos first, empty state when nothing is active), PromptPanel (session
  prompt textarea, preset picker from the existing jailbreak presets API,
  standing-Persona indicator + apply toggle read from the existing
  /api/jailbreak/models map), ParamsPanel (temperature, max tokens),
  ChatThread (streaming render, stop via AbortController, per-reply meta
  line: model + latency + req id). Conversation state is browser-only;
  the full history is sent each turn. API client gains
  `getPlaygroundModels` + `playgroundChatStream` in web/src/api/client.ts.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` green and `go vet ./internal/handlers/...` clean via
  the heavy gate (covers the new dashboard→chat import: no cycle).
- Temporary probe `TestProbePlaygroundPromptPrecedence` (single named
  test, run alone, file deleted after, absence confirmed in git status):
  PASS on all four legs at the applyJailbreak seam with a repo-less
  handler — session-prompt override injects a prepended system message;
  suppression-only override leaves the body untouched; no override with a
  nil repo is a safe no-op; a chat-mode preset doc injects its turns
  through the same machinery. The models aggregation could not be
  exercised the same way (the Repo is a concrete PostgreSQL-backed type
  with no fake), so it reuses `appendConnectionModels` verbatim and was
  verified by build + code-path identity with /v1/models.
- Web build via heavy (`tsc -b && vite build` + precompress) green;
  svelte-check (`--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`) at the standing
  baseline: 89 errors / 56 warnings, zero mentions of the new files.
- Grep proof of no second implementation: `injectSystemPrompt` exists
  only in internal/handlers/chat/jailbreak.go, and the playground chat
  handler's only dispatch is `h.HandleChatCompletions`.
- No existing test files were edited (nav.test.ts reads NAV_ORDER
  generically; the new id needs no mechanical expectation updates).

## [v1.9.36] - 2026-11-08

### Removed

- **Credential vault (envelope encryption at rest) removed; the Security page is now Guardrails only.** The vault was opt-in via `ROUTER_MASTER_KEY` and disabled on the staging install (status: `enabled:false`, 0 sealed / 19 plaintext connections), so it added a master-key failure mode — lose the key, lose every sealed credential — without protecting anything in practice.

**Symptom.** The dashboard's Security page mixed two unrelated systems: an opt-in credential vault (status card, sealed/plaintext counters, master-key rotation) and the guardrail policy engine. The vault was off unless an operator set `ROUTER_MASTER_KEY`, and its seal/hydrate passes sat on every provider-connection read and write.

**Root cause.** The F-5 vault was built as an optional layer: with no master key it degraded to plaintext pass-through, so the fleet ran unsealed while the UI, routes (`GET /api/vault/status`, `POST /api/vault/rotate`), boot migration, and per-write sealing code all stayed in the tree. The owner ordered the system deleted outright rather than enabled.

**Fix.**
- Backend: deleted `internal/vault/`, `internal/db/vault.go` (seal/open call sites, sealed-slot schema columns), `internal/db/vault_migrate.go` (boot-time plaintext-sealing pass), and `internal/handlers/dashboard/vault.go` with both vault routes in both routers. `Repo` no longer carries a vault; connection writes (`CreateProviderConnection`, `CreateProviderConnectionFull`, `ReplaceProviderConnectionPayload`, `UpdateConnectionData`, importer writes) store the `data` payload directly and reads return it as stored — the same plain form a vault-less install always used. The six sealed columns are no longer added to fresh schemas (existing databases keep the now-unused columns; nothing reads them). The vault-only test files went with the feature.
- Guardrails are untouched: policies, audit logs, prompt scanning, and the `guardrailsEnabled` setting behave exactly as before.
- Frontend: the panel loses the vault section (status card, sealed/plaintext summary cards, rotation form and confirm dialog) and the `getVaultStatus`/`rotateVault` API client methods. `SecurityPanel.svelte` is renamed `GuardrailsPanel.svelte`; the tab id `security` becomes `guardrails`, the sidebar label and page titles read "Guardrails", the canonical route is `/dashboard/guardrails`, and the old `/dashboard/security` + `/security` paths remain as legacy aliases. Saved nav preferences carrying the old id are dropped by the existing unknown-id filter, so no preference migration is needed.

**Verification.** `go build ./...` green; `go vet` clean on the touched packages (`internal/db`, `internal/app`, `internal/handlers/...`); web build green; svelte-check at the standing baseline (89 errors / 56 warnings). No `vault` references remain in Go or web sources outside historical changelog/fragments and planning docs. Live staging check before removal: vault disabled, zero sealed rows — so no stored credential is stranded by the removal and no data migration was required.

## [v1.9.35] - 2026-11-07

# 1005 — Stall-timeout progress now reported on every serving path, not just antigravity/gemini

## Symptom

Fragment 1004 turned the combo response timeout into a stall timer, but
progress was only reported from the two chat-handler paths that had manual
ping call sites (the generic forwarder and the Gemini-native handler).
Every other route a combo candidate can take stayed invisible to the
gate: the Responses streaming bridge reads the upstream inside the
executor package, the executor fleet (Responses-format OpenCode lanes,
Azure, Commandcode, the browser-web providers, Trae, Windsurf, Freebuff,
the stealth transport) reads bodies the chat package never touches, and
the single-shot JSON body reads — including the antigravity unwrap — sat
inside one `io.ReadAll` with no sign of life after the arrival ping. A
healthy-but-slow candidate on any of those paths could still be cut at
the silence window while its body was in fact trickling, and a stalled
one was indistinguishable from it.

## Root cause

The progress helper (`noteUpstreamProgress`) and the gate's context key
were unexported inside `internal/handlers/chat`, so no other package
could report progress; and progress was wired per call site instead of
at the point each path receives its response body — so any path nobody
had hand-pinged simply never reported.

## Fix

- The registry moved to where the other request-context keys already
  live: `internal/log` now owns `ProgressGate` (the one-method interface),
  `RegisterProgressGate`, `NoteUpstreamProgress`, and `ProgressReader`.
  The combo gate registers through it in `combo_timeout.go`; chat's
  `noteUpstreamProgress` delegates to the same registry. There is exactly
  one registry mechanism — the chat-local key and interface are gone.
- `log.ProgressReader(ctx, body)` returns a body wrapper that notes
  progress on every `Read` returning bytes. When the context carries no
  gate it returns the body unwrapped, so direct requests and a combo's
  last candidate are byte-for-byte unaffected.
- The wrapper is applied at the response-receipt point of every serving
  path a combo candidate can take: the shared sender `proxy.DoRequest`
  (which covers `ForwardOpenAI`, the Codex/Kiro/Iflow/Kimchi/Grok-CLI
  helpers, Bedrock, ZCode, Qoder, Zed, Minimax-Code and every executor
  built on them), the Gemini-native receipt in the chat handler (covers
  `ForwardGemini`'s internal signature retries, the non-stream read and
  the antigravity unwrap read), and each executor that dials on its own:
  Azure and Commandcode (`providers.go`), the OpenCode stealth transport,
  Trae's session POST and events stream, Windsurf, Freebuff's
  `DoFreebuffHTTP`, and the DeepSeek/Gemini/Grok web completion receipts.
  Downstream consumers — the Responses bridge, the Claude-messages
  translation stream, the codebuddy SSE lane — read bodies received at
  those points, so their reads now report too. The existing handler pings
  in `forward.go` and `gemini_handler.go` are unchanged.
- Gate semantics are untouched: silence-only cut, permanent disarm on
  commit, no resurrection after expiry, benching/grace and the
  last-candidate exemption exactly as before.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` green; `go vet` clean on `internal/log`,
  `internal/handlers/chat`, `internal/proxy`, `internal/proxy/executor`.
- Temporary probe `TestProbeProgressReader` in `internal/log` (created,
  run alone, then deleted): a gate-registered context over a chunked
  reader produced exactly one progress note per chunk with bytes intact;
  a gateless context returned the original body unwrapped with identical
  bytes; a pinged gate outlived its 80 ms window across five chunks
  30 ms apart while a silent gate expired.

## [v1.9.34] - 2026-11-07

# 1004 — Combo response timeout is now a stall timer: only total upstream silence is cut

## Symptom

A combo "auto" attempt (antigravity / gemini-3.8-flash, ~104k-token prompt
after compression) received its upstream response headers at 118.5s — the
upstream was alive, just slow to first token on a huge prompt — but had
committed no output when the combo's 120-second response timeout fired.
The attempt was canceled, recorded as a 499 "context canceled" attempt
row, and the combo fell back. For the owner's workload (coding: long
streams, contexts above 100k tokens, slow first tokens are normal) this
kept sacrificing healthy attempts at an arbitrary wall-clock line.

## Root cause

`comboResponseTimeout` ran one absolute deadline from attempt start
(`time.AfterFunc(timeout, expire)`). It knew only two states — committed
and not — and had no notion of upstream progress: response headers, body
chunks read while translation buffered them, and a genuinely dead
upstream were indistinguishable to the timer, so all three died at the
same instant.

## Fix

- `FirstTokenTimeoutMs` is now the maximum tolerated upstream SILENCE.
  The timer starts at attempt start and restarts in full on every
  upstream progress signal; it still cancels only an uncommitted
  candidate, and once output commits it is disarmed exactly as before.
  The setting name, `comboTimeoutPolicy`, the grace/benching semantics,
  and the last-candidate exemption are unchanged — only the meaning of
  the window moved from "time since start" to "time since last sign of
  life".
- The gate stores its timeout and learns `Progress()` (mutex-guarded
  `timer.Reset`, a no-op once committed, and deliberately unable to
  resurrect an expired gate). The gate registers itself in its own
  derived context under an unexported key; the new `noteUpstreamProgress`
  helper pings whatever gate a context carries and no-ops otherwise, so
  direct (non-combo) requests are completely unaffected.
- Progress call sites, one ping per event: the Gemini-native forwarder
  when the upstream response headers arrive and on every chunk the
  streaming loop reads (including chunks translation buffers before any
  client write); the generic forwarder when the upstream response
  arrives and on every chunk read in its stream handlers (Claude-upstream
  translation, passthrough, and OpenAI→Claude translation).
- Copy follows the semantics: the `FirstTokenTimeoutMs` field comment
  and the combo editor's shared help text (`RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_HELP`) now
  describe a silence window — "any sign of life restarts the clock" —
  instead of a first-response deadline.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` green; `go vet` clean on `internal/handlers/chat` and
  `internal/db`; edited files gofmt-clean.
- A temporary probe (`TestProbeStallTimer`, run once and deleted)
  asserted the new semantics directly: an 80ms gate pinged every 30ms
  five times (~150ms total) stayed alive and its Write committed; a
  silent 60ms gate expired and a late ping did not resurrect it; the
  helper no-ops on a gate-less context.
- Web build green; svelte-check at the standing baseline (89 errors /
  56 warnings, unchanged).

## [v1.9.33] - 2026-11-07

# 1003 — One log axis: request ID + serving account on every serving-path line

## Symptom

The middleware has minted a request ID (`req_<hex12>`) all along and the
access line prints it, but nothing else did: the `[gemini]`, `[usage]`,
`[proxy]` and `[fallback]` lines of the very same request carried no ID
at all, and no account name either — the `log.*Ctx` helpers that prepend
the ID existed with zero call sites in the chat handlers. Following one
request through the console meant eyeballing timestamps, which collide
under parallel bursts, and a stored request detail shared no identifier
with the log trail, so the two could never be joined exactly.

## Fix

- `internal/log` gains the account half of the axis, mirroring the
  request-ID pattern: `WithAccount(ctx, name)` / `AccountFromContext(ctx)`
  under a typed `AccountKey`. `outputCtx` now prepends `req_id` first and
  `account` second, ahead of the caller's own fields, on every `*Ctx`
  line. An empty account stays absent rather than rendering blank.
- The serving path stamps the account per attempt:
  `tryForwardWithConnection` wraps its context with the attempt's
  connection display name (`withConnAccount`: `connObjName`, falling back
  to the stored email — for antigravity the name is the account email)
  before anything derives from it, and the fallback loop stamps its
  post-attempt lines the same way, so each hop of a combo/fallback trail
  names the account that actually served it.
- 55 plain log calls on the serving trail converted to their `*Ctx`
  variants: the fallback loop and attempt body (client-cancel,
  upstream-failed, connection-locked, rotation lines), the Gemini-native
  forwarder (upstream response headers, stream ended, translate errors),
  the generic forwarder's stream/JSON handlers, token-saver lines, and
  the `[usage] logged` line itself.
- Proxy resolution joins the axis: `getClientForConnectionCtx` threads
  the request context through the pool pick / no-fit-pool / strict-mode
  lines; the context-free `getClientForConnection` remains for probes and
  admin callers and logs unadorned, as before.
- Request details record the axis: both chat-path detail payloads
  (success and failure) now carry `reqId` from the request context when
  one is present (absent, never zero-filled, on ID-less paths), and
  `models.RequestDetail` gains the matching `ReqID` field
  (`reqId,omitempty`). Rows stored earlier simply omit it.
- `GET /api/console-logs` accepts `?requestId=req_…` and returns only the
  lines containing that ID — one substring match catches both the access
  line's `id=` and the axis's `req_id=`. The SSE stream accepts the same
  parameter for its init dump and live lines. `?n=` caps the result to
  the last n entries and is applied **after** the filter, so it always
  means "the last n lines of the filtered trail".
- No dashboard change: the console page renders line text verbatim (and
  its search box now doubles as a request-ID filter).

## [v1.9.32] - 2026-11-07

# 1002 — Proxy badge: repeated-prefix hardening

## Symptom

With the provider strategy stored as `proxyGroup = "group:ISP-BD"`
(the selector form), every Antigravity account badge painted red
("inactive") while traffic was verifiably flowing through the group:
the provider page derived its lock selector by unconditional
prefixing, producing `group:group:ISP-BD` — a group name no pool
carries — and the per-account badge's provider fallback stripped
only one prefix, counting pools in a group literally named
"group:ISP-BD".

## Fix

- The provider lock derivation (ProviderDetailView) and the NoAuth
  proxy card now build the selector with the shared
  `normalizeProxyTarget` (`web/src/lib/proxyBindings.ts`, mirroring
  the backend's `db.NormalizeProxyTarget`): an already-prefixed value
  passes through, a bare known type becomes a type selector, any
  other bare value becomes a group selector — per comma-separated
  part, so multi-group values derive correctly too.
- The badge's provider fallback strips repeated `group:`/`type:`
  prefixes (`/^((group|type):)+/`), so even a double-prefixed value
  stored by an older build or by hand still resolves to the real
  group name and counts its pools.
- The badge's selector parser (shared `parseProxyTargetParts`) takes
  a part's kind from its first prefix and strips any further ones,
  so a hardened value can never re-enter the count under a
  prefix-carrying name.
- The per-connection dropdown's "Auto:" line now renders the derived
  lock label ("Auto: Group X", "Auto: Groups A + B") instead of
  stripping one prefix inline.

## Verification

- svelte-check at the pristine baseline totals (89 errors /
  56 warnings) with no diagnostic referencing the new helpers;
  `bun run build` green.

# 1001 — Proxy bindings: multi-group / multi-selector targets

## Symptom

A proxy binding named exactly one pool, one type, or one group. An
operator who wanted an account or a whole provider to rotate across
two groups (e.g. a primary ISP group plus a fallback group) had to
merge the pools under one tag, losing the grouping, or bind different
accounts to different groups and give up the shared rotation.

## Fix

The binding target now accepts a comma-separated list of selectors,
resolved as their union everywhere a target is consumed:

- `Repo.ActivePoolsByTarget` splits the target
  (`db.SplitProxyTarget`: parts trimmed, blank and `__none__` parts
  dropped) and unions each part's matches, deduplicated by pool ID in
  first-seen order. A single-part target goes through the exact
  pre-change matching code, so existing bindings behave identically.
- `db.NormalizeProxyTarget` is the one stored-value derivation —
  per part: an explicit `group:`/`type:` prefix passes through, a
  bare known type becomes a type selector, any other bare value
  becomes a group selector. The chat resolver
  (`resolveProviderProxyPoolID`) and the dashboard proxy-resolution
  readout both call it, so a stored multi value (`A,B`) reaches the
  matcher as `group:A,group:B` at both surfaces instead of the
  mangled single `group:A,B`.
- The per-connection client/relay resolution treats any target
  containing a comma as a selector target (a pool ID can never
  contain one), so a multi binding stored on a connection reaches
  `ActivePoolsByTarget` intact instead of failing as a missing pool.
- The resolution readout reports the union's candidates and labels
  the binding `group` when every part is a group, `type` when every
  part is a type, `pool` for a lone pool ID, and `multi` when mixed.
- Per-account badge (`proxyBadge.ts`): a multi-selector binding
  counts active pools across the union and reads e.g.
  "Groups: A + B (35)"; a mixed group+type target reads "Multi:".
- Add-connection modal: a "Select multiple groups" mode replaces the
  proxy select with a checkbox list of groups and stores the combined
  selector in the same `proxyPoolId` field; one checked group stores
  exactly today's `group:<name>` value. Types stay single there.
- Provider lock: the header control is now a popover — groups are
  checkboxes (multi-select, applied per toggle), types remain
  single-select and replace the group selection. The writer keeps the
  canonical pair: `proxyPoolId` carries the full selector and
  `proxyGroup` mirrors the bare name(s), comma-joined when the lock
  names several groups.

Stored-value contract: a multi-group binding is
`proxyPoolId = "group:A,group:B"` with
`proxyGroup = "A,B"` (provider lock) or the full selector alone
(per-connection `proxyPoolId`).

## Verification

- Temporary in-package probe (created, run, deleted) against the
  local staging PostgreSQL: single group/type/pool-ID/inactive and
  bare targets returned exactly the pre-change sets; unions,
  first-seen ordering, group+type overlap dedupe, self-dedupe,
  `__none__`-part handling, and the split/normalize derivations all
  matched expectations, including a normalize-then-resolve pass for a
  bare multi proxyGroup.
- `go build ./...` green; `bun run build` green; svelte-check at the
  pristine baseline totals (89 errors / 56 warnings).

# 997 — Proxy Pools: batch import takes four formats and imports partially

## Symptom

The batch import accepted only two line formats
(`protocol://user:pass@host:port` and `host:port:user:pass`), created
pools one serial request at a time, and — worst — aborted the entire
paste when any single line was invalid.

## Fix

Frontend only (`web/src/lib/proxy-import.ts` + the import flow):

- The parser additionally accepts `user:pass@host:port` and bare
  `host:port` (http assumed for both scheme-less forms), bracketed IPv6
  hosts in every scheme-less form, and validates ports (numeric,
  1–65535). Stored URLs are canonicalised through `URL` as before.

  lines are counted, reported with reasons, and left in the textarea for
  fixing instead of discarding the whole paste.
- Deduplication now also covers duplicates inside the paste itself
  (previously only against existing pools).
- Creates run with bounded concurrency (chunks of 8) instead of strictly
  serially.

## Verification

  no-test-suites-before-production rule it was not run; the two original

## [v1.9.27] - 2026-11-07

# 990 — Realtime table: provider folds under the model, new API Key column (key name + client IP)

## Symptom

The owner asked for two changes to the Usage page's realtime table:
merge the Provider column into the Model column with the provider shown
underneath the model, and add a new column carrying the client API key
that was used — its name, and the IP the call came from.

## Root cause

The layout half was a straight table restructure, but the data half did
not exist. The detail payload's `apiKey` field is the UPSTREAM provider
credential the request used (that is what attributed requests to backend
accounts; the caller's key was only ever recorded, masked, on the usage
history row for per-key budgets). The client key's NAME and the client
IP were recorded nowhere in the request details: the name never left the
auth middleware's context value, and the IP was never resolved on the
gateway path at all — the product's resolver (`auth.LoginClientIP`) was
only used by the dashboard login.

## Fix

Backend:
- The three gateway entry points that already stamp the dispatching key
  onto the context (chat completions, messages, responses) now also
  stamp the resolved client IP via a new `withClientIP` /
  `clientIPFromContext` pair (`client_ip.go`), resolved by
  `requestClientIP` through `auth.LoginClientIP` — the one sanctioned
  resolver (edge-stamped real IP with peer proof, TRUSTED_PROXIES /
  TRUST_PROXY chains, Cloudflare when trusted, else the socket address).
- Both detail payload builders (success and failure) merge
  `callerDetailFields(ctx)`: `apiKeyName` and the masked `clientApiKey`
  from the authenticated key in context, plus `clientIp`. Absent pieces
  stay absent — a keyless caller has nothing to record. The existing
  `apiKey` field is untouched.
- The detail list layer extracts the three fields
  (`RequestDetailListRow` + select + scan) and `detailListItem` emits
  them (`apiKeyName`, `clientApiKey`, `clientIp`, all omitempty). Rows
  written before this change read as empty, which the UI renders as "—"
  rather than inventing a caller.

Frontend (`AxonRealtime.svelte` + types):
- The Provider column is gone. The Model cell now stacks: the model
  line, and underneath it the provider badge with the STREAM/JSON chip
  from fragment 989.
- A new API Key column sits after Upstream Account: the key's name on
  the first line (the masked key when the key has no name, "—" when
  there was no key), and the client IP in small mono underneath.
- Mobile cards gain a "Key: <name> · <ip>" line when the row carries
  caller data; the card search now also matches key name, masked key,
  and IP.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` over the touched packages are clean;
  gofmt clean.
- svelte-check (with `--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`) totals identical
  to the pristine baseline (89 errors / 56 warnings, zero new) and the
  web build succeeds.
- The caller chain is the one the codebase already trusts: the
  authenticated key object the auth middleware injects (the same source
  the per-key budget accounting reads), and the login path's IP
  resolver. Live pixel proof rides on the next staging view, like 988
  and 989 — the column populates from real gateway traffic, which no
  environment reachable from here can stage on demand.

# 989 — STREAM/JSON mode information on the Usage page, wired from the dispatch layer

## Symptom

The owner asked for the stream-or-JSON information AxonRouter JS shows on
its Usage page: a STREAM/JSON chip on each in-flight card, mode pills
(Stream n / JSON n) on the realtime card, and the mode carried by the
request rows. The Go port had deliberately omitted all of it (recorded
in the 907 parity notes) because no Go usage surface recorded the mode:
the field existed on the recent-request wire type and was populated
nowhere.

## Root cause

The information died at the dispatch boundary. The forwarder knows the
mode (`forwardRequestParams.IsStream`, parsed from the client's
request), but `UsageLogInfo` — the struct every usage surface reads —
carried no such field, the in-flight tracker aggregated its counters
without a mode dimension, and the stored request-detail payloads never
recorded it. Three surfaces, one missing wire.

## Fix

Backend:
- `shared.UsageLogInfo` gains `IsStream`; all three constructions in
  `tryForwardWithConnection` (success, failure, proxy-pool failure) set
  it from the forwarder's own flag.
- In-flight tracker: `TrackPendingRequested` takes the mode and keeps
  two shadow counter families (`pending/modelstream/`,
  `pending/acctstream/`) incremented with the same deltas as the totals.
  `buildPayload` splits each aggregate key into up to two rows — the
  streaming share and the rest — clamped so a leaked counter can never
  report more streaming requests than the key holds; a drained account
  pair deletes its shadow, and a drained model key deletes its own.
  `ActiveRequest.isStream` is emitted without omitempty: on a live row,
  false is information. The `/api/usage/active-requests` shape passes it
  through.
- Completed requests: both `PushRecent` sites (success and failure) set
  `RecentRequest.IsStream` from the log info, and both stored detail
  payloads (success and failure) record `"isStream"`.
- Detail list: `RequestDetailListRow` extracts the flag from the stored
  payload; rows written before it existed read as true — upstream's own
  default for an unrecorded mode (`chatCore/requestDetail.js`:
  `isStream ?? true`). `detailListItem` emits it on every row.

Frontend:
- The in-flight modal card draws upstream's ModeBadge (STREAM with the
  wifi_tethering icon / JSON with the code icon, primary chip) at the
  top right, beside the provider alias prefix fragment 988 added.
- The realtime table and its mobile cards show the same chip beside the
  provider badge; the Details tab's Provider cell carries it too.
- The realtime filter pills gain Stream (n) and JSON (n) in the same
  single-select group as All/Success/Failed — upstream's filterType
  model — counting and filtering on the recorded mode.
- Mechanical test fix: three `TrackPendingRequested` call sites in
  `tracker_test.go` gain the new trailing argument (signature change);
  no expectations changed.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` over the touched packages are clean.
- A temporary in-package probe (run, then deleted) drove the tracker
  through the memory store: two streaming + one JSON request on one
  account key plus one streaming direct request produced exactly the
  split rows {account ×2 STREAM, account ×1 JSON, direct ×1 STREAM},
  and finishing the streaming requests drained only their rows.
- svelte-check (with `--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`) totals identical
  to the pristine baseline (89 errors / 56 warnings, zero new) and the
  web build succeeds.
- Pixel proof rides on the next staging view, like 988: the chips render
  from live traffic and recorded rows, which no environment reachable
  from here can stage on demand.

# 988 — In-flight cards draw the provider as upstream's alias prefix, not a grey pill

## Symptom

The owner screenshotted the Usage page's Active In-Flight Requests modal:
each card led with a bare model line and a small grey pill whose text was
a fragment-like word ("Trust", "Wz") — the custom node's name, presented
with no context — above an unlabelled "Account: …" line. He asked for the
streaming view's provider badge to be updated to the AxonRouter JS
standard.

## Root cause

The Go port invented its own card: model line, then a detached pill
rendering `providerDisplayName(provider)`. Upstream's ActiveRequestsModal
never had such a pill — it renders the provider as a coloured alias
prefix on the model line itself (`formatProviderModel`: "alias/model",
the alias in the primary colour and semibold), over a labelled card:
a "MODEL" micro-label above the model line, and an account footer
separated by a hairline carrying an icon, an "ACCOUNT:" micro-label and
the value. The pill was also the only place the provider appeared, so a
short node name read as a stray fragment instead of an identity.

## Fix

Frontend only (`AxonRealtime.svelte` + one helper in analytics/types.ts):

- New `providerAlias()`: the catalog alias when the registry carries one
  (the same lookup chain `providerDisplayName` uses), else the display
  name — so a custom compatible node still reads as itself, never as its
  raw synthetic id.
- The in-flight card now mirrors upstream's structure: "MODEL" label
  with icon; the model line as `alias/` in primary semibold followed by
  the model, with a redundant alias/provider prefix stripped from the
  model the way upstream strips it, and the full display name plus
  combo label in the title; below a hairline, the account footer with
  icon and "ACCOUNT:" label, the ×count and the (conditional) elapsed
  time right-aligned. The grid gains upstream's fourth column at `xl`.
- The grey provider pill is gone from the modal. The completed-requests
  table and mobile cards keep their full-name Provider badge — there the
  name has a labelled column and reads correctly.

Deliberately not drawn: upstream's STREAM/JSON mode chip. Go's tracker
aggregates in-flight requests into counted (model, provider, account)
rows with no stream flag and no per-request start time, so the chip
would be decoration over nothing — the standing honesty rule for this
card, unchanged. Elapsed time still renders when a row happens to carry
a start time, as before.

## Verification

- svelte-check (with `--tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json`) totals identical
  to the pristine baseline (89 errors / 56 warnings, zero new) and the
  web build succeeds.
- The card markup is a direct port of upstream ActiveRequestsModal.js's
  card structure, diffed field by field during the audit.
- Pixel confirmation rides on the next staging view with live traffic:
  the modal renders only while requests are in flight, which no
  environment reachable from here can stage on demand. The owner's
  screenshot shows the staging gateway serving OpenCode traffic, so the
  first live open of the modal after deploy is the visual check.

# 987 — Quota rows stack on mobile like upstream; CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy price fields forwarded

## Symptom

The owner asked for the CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy UI to be checked against
AxonRouter JS so it looks as good there. The audit found the family
surfaces already at parity — the Total Credit card, per-pack rows with
the recurring/"expires in" wording, the hide-row action with persisted
visibility, the Provider Detail "Credits left: X / Y (resets …)" line
(verbatim with JS ConnectionRow), and the combo credit ordering — except
for the quota row layout itself at phone width, plus one dropped field
pair in the normalization.

## Root cause

Upstream's QuotaTable row stacks on mobile: the row is a column (name
row, with the reset time riding on it, then the progress block owning a
full row) and only becomes a horizontal row at `sm:` and up. Upstream's
own comment records why: at 360 px the fixed 144 px name column plus the
reset column left the progress column 0–27 px wide and cut the
used/total text to two glyphs. The Go port kept a single horizontal
flex row at every width — the fixed `w-36` name column and the reset
column always present — reproducing exactly that crush for every
provider's rows, CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy packs included. Separately,
upstream's parseQuotaData forwards `price`/`priceNote` for the
codebuddy-cn / codebuddy-intl / workbuddy branches and the shared row
renders a price tagline under the pack name when a price is present;
the Go normalization dropped both fields and the Go row had no tagline
slot. (No CodeBuddy billing response on either side currently sets a
price — upstream's only producer is the FreeBuff usage service — so this
half is plumbing parity: the fields now survive end to end and the
tagline renders the moment a quota carries one.)

## Fix

Frontend only, in the shared quota table (the same component upstream
renders these providers with):

- Row container is `relative flex flex-col gap-1.5 sm:flex-row
  sm:items-center sm:gap-2`; the name cell drops its fixed width below
  `sm:` (`sm:w-36 sm:shrink-0`) and gains a mobile-only reset span
  (`sm:hidden`) showing the same countdown/"expires in" label; the
  progress cell gains `sm:min-w-[7rem]`; the desktop reset cell is
  `hidden sm:block`.
- The hide-row button follows upstream's placement: absolute at the
  row's top-right with a 44 px touch target on mobile, static 32 px at
  `sm:` and up (the row is `relative` to anchor it).
- The name cell gains the price tagline line
  (`formatFreebucksPrice(price)` plus ` · priceNote`, title = priceNote),
  rendered only when the quota carries a price; `formatFreebucksPrice`
  is ported into quota/types.ts, `price`/`priceNote` join
  NormalizedQuota, and the codebuddy-cn / codebuddy-intl / workbuddy
  parse branch forwards both fields.
- Untouched by design: Go's credit-balance row treatment (an amount, no
  bar) and the gray "unknown" color state, both deliberate Go-side
  choices upstream lacks; the Total Credit card; color thresholds
  (>70 green, ≥30 yellow, else red — verified identical to upstream).

## Verification

- svelte-check totals identical to the pristine baseline (89 errors /
  56 warnings, zero new), and the web build succeeds.
- The layout classes are a direct port of upstream QuotaTable.js's row
  markup, diffed line by line during the audit; every other family
  surface named above was read in both trees before concluding parity.
- A pixel-level check of populated CodeBuddy rows remains open by
  environment: no CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy connection exists in any database
  reachable from here, and the rows render only from a live billing
  read, so the first staging view of a real account is the visual
  confirmation. The change is class-level markup in one shared
  component, with no logic altered.

# 986 — Quota reads release quota locks on recovery; MiniMax M Plan windows render as progress

## Symptom

Two gaps around the Quota Tracker, reported by the owner:

1. No automatic release: when a quota check showed an account's quota had
   refilled (the owner's example: a MiniMax Global account whose credits
   were back), the account stayed in cooldown / locked / exhausted until
   the timer lapsed or an operator pressed the manual Reset button.
2. MiniMax providers showed no progress UI: the M Plan rate windows
   arrived in the tracker as nameless rows with no bar, no percentage and
   no reset time, while other providers render a progress bar per window.

## Root cause

1. `HandleGetConnectionUsage` treated a usage read as one-way. Its only
   state writes were for bad news (an Antigravity ToS message disables the
   account; a validation message sets the verification flag). A successful
   read that reported quota available changed nothing — the persisted
   `rateLimitedUntil`, per-model locks and the stored quota error all
   survived it. The only automatic releases in the tree were the chat
   success path (a real generation) and the DeepSeek credential renewal.
2. The MiniMax Code usage port stored each parsed M Plan window in the
   quotas map as the internal `miniMaxCodeWindow` struct, whose fields are
   all unexported — so every window serialized to `{}`. Upstream
   (`open-sse/services/minimaxCodeUsage.js`) emits each window as a full
   quota map (`used: 100-left, total: 100, remainingPercentage: left,
   resetAt`), and the frontend's minimax branch and progress-bar rendering
   were already built for exactly that shape; they simply never received
   the numbers.

## Fix

1. New `usage_autorelease.go`: after a **live** usage fetch succeeds in
   `HandleGetConnectionUsage` (the generic provider path, its
   auth-refresh retry, and the Antigravity path on a message-free read),
   `maybeAutoReleaseQuotaLocks` releases the connection's quota lock state
   when the fresh quotas show availability (any unlimited row, any credit
   balance above zero, or any window with `remainingPercentage > 0`).
   The release re-reads the connection, requires stored evidence of a
   quota-class park (a rate-limit timer, `lockedAllUntil`, a per-model
   lock, or a stored error the provider classifier reads as quota
   exhausted / rate limited), and then calls the same two Repo operations
   the DeepSeek renewal uses: `ClearConnectionRateLimit` (also clears the
   stored error and restores status) and `ClearConnectionModelLocks`.
   Boundaries, all deliberate: a stored ToS-disable signature vetoes the
   release; disabled accounts never reach the fetch (the handler returns
   their stored reason first), nothing is reactivated and no verification
   flag is cleared; cached usage responses return before any fetch, so
   only live reads can release; Antigravity's in-memory strike breaker
   (chat-path layer, self-expiring) is untouched — the persisted state is
   what is released. Failures are logged and never fail the usage
   response.
2. `usage_minimax_code.go`: windows are converted with
   `miniMaxCodeWindowQuota` into the upstream quota shape
   (`usageQuota(100-remaining, 100, resetAt)` plus `name` and
   `remaining`), so the tracker's existing minimax branch now renders the
   progress bar, percentage and reset countdown per window. The credits
   row is unchanged: MiniMax reports a balance with no grant total, so it
   stays an amount (`isCreditBalance`) rather than an invented
   percentage.

## Verification

- Temporary in-package probe (run, then removed): availability evaluation
  (MiniMax window with quota left → available; all windows at zero → not;
  credits balance > 0 → available; balance 0 → not; unlimited → available),
  lock-state gate (rate-limit timer → release; model lock → release;
  stored "quota exceeded" error → release; stored ToS signature →
  vetoed; clean data → no release), and the window conversion (remaining
  80 → used 20 / total 100 / remainingPercentage 80, name and resetAt
  preserved).
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the touched package clean. No frontend
  files change; the svelte-check totals are unchanged.
- Live proof with a real MiniMax account remains open by environment, not
  by code: no MiniMax connection exists in any database reachable from
  here, so the first staging read of a locked-then-refilled MiniMax
  account is the live check. The probe covers the decision logic; the
  fetch itself is the pre-existing port, unchanged except for the window
  payload shape, which the probe pins to upstream's.

## [v1.9.26] - 2026-11-07

# 985 — Usage Overview presence effect loops forever (effect_update_depth_exceeded) while requests are in flight

## Symptom

Opening the Usage Overview while the gateway was serving traffic
threw an uncaught `effect_update_depth_exceeded` (Svelte) and the
view died. With no request in flight the page loaded fine, which is
why it survived staging checks that ran against an idle gateway.

## Root cause

The topology presence effect in AnalyticsView.svelte stamps
providers from `Date.now()` (active requests, pulses) and then, in
the same effect, merges them into the `observedActivity` state —
reading it (`new Map(observedActivity)`) and writing it back
(`observedActivity = next`). The read subscribes the effect to the
very state it writes, and the merge's "only strictly newer stamps"
guard can never stop the cycle: the stamp source is the current
time, so every pass produces a newer stamp, `changed` is always
true, the write re-triggers the effect, and Svelte aborts after the
update-depth limit. The errorProvider leg of the same effect had
already been fixed for this exact pattern (stamp only on change,
review cycle 3 A-1); the active-request and pulse legs kept the
stamp-with-now behaviour.

## Fix (web/src/components/analytics/AnalyticsView.svelte)

- The merge block now runs inside `untrack(...)`: growing
  `observedActivity` from its previous value is bookkeeping, not a
  reactive dependency. The effect re-runs on its real inputs only
  (activeRequests, pulseProvider, errorProvider, stats recent rows),
  the stamps still merge monotonically, and the five-minute presence
  expiry (driven by the separate topologyNow clock and the
  topologyProviders derivation) is unchanged.

## Verification

- The loop is provable from the code alone: tracked read + write of
  one $state in a single effect whose guard compares against an
  always-advancing clock. The fix removes the subscription, so the
  cycle cannot form; presence semantics (who is stamped, when they
  expire) are byte-for-byte the same inputs and outputs.
- svelte-check: 89 errors / 56 warnings before and after; the
  normalized error set is identical except four pre-existing
  AnalyticsView errors at line numbers shifted by the insertion.
  Zero new errors.
- `bun run build` succeeds (bundle + pre-compression complete).

## [v1.9.25] - 2026-11-07

# 984 — Capacity 503s no longer borrow quota reset durations (cooldown bounded to the backoff class)

## Symptom

On the JS router (production, 2026-11-07), one account's 503 "no
capacity available for model" benched the model fleet-wide for ~2
hours: the capacity writer copied an hours-long lock duration that
followed an upstream reset hint, instead of the 60–120s window a
capacity signal is supposed to earn, and no successful dial cleared
it. Fixed there in v0.1.34 by clamping the capacity writer.

The Go router had the same defect in a different shape. For every
non-429 retryable status, `retryableCooldownSec` replaced the
classifier's backoff with a reset duration extracted from the error
body (`quotaResetDelay` metadata or "resets in …" text), capped only
at 72h. A 503 is a capacity/node verdict, but a reset duration found
in its body describes a different window (a quota reset) — so one
capacity response could park an account (the fallback handler writes
an account-level rate-limit lock for non-model-scoped errors) for
hours, far beyond the capacity class's own 2s→5min backoff.

## Fix (internal/handlers/chat/retry_after.go)

- `retryableCooldownSec` no longer consults `extractResetDuration`
  for status 503: a 503 cooldown is always the classifier's backoff
  (Backoff class, 2s doubling capped at 5min), the same short window
  the JS fix clamps to. `cooldownSecForClassification` is the single
  entry point for both failover loops (fallback and combo), so one
  change covers both.
- Scope is deliberately narrow: 429 handling (Retry-After / RetryInfo
  honoured in both directions) and the reset-duration reading for
  every other status are unchanged, as are the model-scoped quota
  paths (a 503 whose body carries QUOTA_EXHAUSTED /
  MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED markers still routes model-scoped before
  this function is reached) and the banned/exhausted unclamped
  classes.
- Known remaining difference from the JS fix: JS also clears its
  provider-wide model bench on a successful dial. Go's locks are
  per-account + per-model rather than provider-wide, and with the
  duration bounded to the backoff they expire in minutes, so no
  success-clearing path is added here.

## Verification

- Temporary in-package probe (run, passed, deleted):
  cooldownSecForClassification with synthetic upstream errors —
  503 + body carrying quotaResetDelay 7200s → 2s (was 7200s before
  the fix); 503 plain overloaded body → 2s; 503 at the backoff cap →
  300s; 429 + Retry-After 7200 header → 7200 (unchanged); 403 + the
  same reset body → 7200 (unchanged, scope discipline).
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the touched package: clean.

## [v1.9.24] - 2026-11-07

# 983 — Antigravity exchange: restore client_secret alongside PKCE (982's no-secret assumption falsified live)

## Symptom

Add-account sign-ins with the v1.9.23 flow failed at the final step:
the dashboard exchange returned 502 "token exchange returned status
400". The 982 change had been verified only against a local token stub,
which accepted the no-secret form. The real Google endpoint does not.

## Root cause

Fragment 982 assumed agy's client is a public installed-app client
whose exchange proves possession of the PKCE verifier INSTEAD of a
client secret. That assumption is wrong for this client: the live
token endpoint rejects a secret-less authorization_code exchange for
it even when the PKCE verifier matches. The same assumption was
falsified independently on the JS router and fixed there (v0.1.33) by
sending the embedded secret again; pre-982 Go always sent the secret
and its add-account flow worked.

## Fix (internal/handlers/oauth/antigravity.go)

- The exchange form once again sends `client_secret` — the value the
  provider config already carries (`getAntigravityOAuthConfig`), the
  public secret embedded in agy itself — TOGETHER WITH the PKCE
  `code_verifier` from 982. Nothing else in the flow changes:
  authorize (pinned Google redirect, per-request S256 challenge,
  server-side single-use verifier store), the {code, state}
  requirement, post-token behavior (972 identity pinning), and the
  refresh path are all exactly as 982 left them.
- The non-200 log line now records Google's error body. Error bodies
  carry only error/error_description — never tokens — and a bare
  status code made this failure undiagnosable from the server log.
  Success bodies are still never logged.

## Verification (live, decisive)

- 2026-11-07 13:30 WIB: a real authorization code from a real sign-in
  exchanged against the UNPATCHED v1.9.23 build → Google 400
  (reproduced a second time at 13:35 through an operator restart
  error; that run is not evidence about the patch).
- 2026-11-07 13:39 WIB: a fresh real code exchanged against the
  patched build → HTTP 200, connection created for the signed-in
  account. The exchange leg is proven end-to-end on the real
  endpoint.
- Mechanical test update (edited, not run — standing rule):
  antigravity_test.go's mock token endpoint now REQUIRES a non-empty
  client_secret (mirroring the live endpoint) instead of rejecting
  its presence.
- Not covered by this proof: generation with the new account's
  tokens from the build VM (its upstream DNS resolves to a reserved
  range and the SSRF guard blocks the dial before egress). The
  generation leg is verified on the hijilaptop staging instance,
  whose egress is normal.

## [v1.9.23] - 2026-11-07

# 982 — Antigravity add-account login mirrors agy /login (PKCE + paste-code)

The Antigravity sign-in was the last surface still telling a different
story from agy: it rode the inherited dashboard-callback flow. It now
mirrors agy's /login on all three points where they differed. Scope is
Antigravity ONLY — every other provider's OAuth flow, the shared
/callback page, and the oauth-handoff machinery are untouched.

## What agy does (proven)

- Authorize URL: client_id 1071006060591-…,
  redirect_uri=https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback (a Google-hosted
  page that DISPLAYS the authorization code for manual copy-paste), PKCE
  S256, scopes in agy order, access_type=offline, prompt=consent, state.
  (Runtime capture, teardown §7; Ricki's own URL capture 2026-11-07.)
- Exchange: code + code_verifier + that same redirect_uri; NO
  client_secret — the client is a public installed-app client.

## What changed

### Authorize (internal/handlers/oauth/antigravity.go)

- redirect_uri is FIXED to the new constant `antigravityRedirectURI`
  (internal/handlers/oauth/antigravity_pkce.go). A client-supplied
  ?redirect_uri= is no longer honored for this provider; the old
  `getAntigravityRedirectURI` helper is deleted.
- Per request the handler mints a PKCE pair (the package's established
  `pkceVerifier()` / `sha256Base64()` primitives) and adds
  code_challenge + code_challenge_method=S256 to the URL. Client id,
  scope list/order, access_type, prompt and state semantics are
  unchanged; the ?redirect=true variant still works; the JSON response
  still returns the URL + state, with redirectUri now the fixed Google
  page.

### Verifier storage (internal/handlers/oauth/antigravity_pkce.go, new)

- Process-wide store keyed by state, TTL 10 minutes, single-use
  (consume deletes unconditionally, before the token call, so a replayed
  state can never ride a second attempt; expired entries report as
  missing).
- Why not the existing PKCE machinery: the generic handlers
  (pkce.go/cline.go) hand verifier custody to the CLIENT — their
  authorize JSON returns codeVerifier and the exchange reads it back
  from the request body. agy's flow never exposes the verifier to the
  client, and this provider's exchange is bespoke (it also owns
  projectId preservation and the fragment-972 identity pin), so it
  cannot ride completePKCEExchange/persistConnection. The store is the
  smallest equivalent inside the oauth package and deliberately follows
  the Codex session registry's shape (mutex-guarded map, TTL sweep on
  write, drop-on-read).

### Exchange (internal/handlers/oauth/antigravity.go)

- Accepts {code, state} (the pasted-code path via cleanAuthCode is
  unchanged, including full-URL pastes). Missing code → 400; missing
  state → 400; unknown/expired/reused state → 400.
- The token form is now {code, client_id, redirect_uri =
  antigravityRedirectURI (server-side constant), grant_type,
  code_verifier} — NO client_secret. A client-supplied redirectUri
  field is still parsed (older dashboard builds do not break) but never
  honored.
- Everything after a successful token response is functionally
  identical: connID derivation, the data map, projectId preservation,
  and the fragment-972 identity pin (existing pin carried verbatim,
  fresh snapshot for new/unpinned connections).
- The refresh path is NOT touched: fragment 970's dual-config refresher
  lives in internal/proxy/oauth and reads its own configs from
  internal/providers; KnownOAuthConfigs is unchanged.

### Axon-compat dispatch (internal/handlers/oauth/batch3_dynamic2.go)

- dynExchange now threads the client's state into the delegated
  Antigravity payload (the handler consumes the verifier by state) and
  Antigravity joins the gate's no-client-codeVerifier set, since its
  verifier is server-side now. The gate's redirectUri requirement for
  the compat route is unchanged.

### Frontend (web/src/api/client.ts, ProviderDetailView.svelte)

- client.getAntigravityAuthorizeUrl() takes no redirectUri anymore;
  client.antigravityExchange(code, state) posts only {code, state}.
- The modal is the paste-code pattern with the layout Ricki confirmed
  (2026-11-07): the login step shows (1) the login URL itself in a
  readable field, (2) an explicit "Open login page" button that opens
  the new tab ONLY on a manual click, and (3) a Copy button for the
  URL — plus the paste-code field and Connect. Pressing Add / Log in
  must NOT auto-open a tab: the previous window.open in
  openAntigravityOAuth is removed (other providers keep their
  auto-open; this requirement is Antigravity-only). The banner,
  divider, step-2 label, placeholder and helper text instruct the user
  that Google's Antigravity page will display a code to copy and paste
  here, then Connect.
- The dashboard /callback auto-handoff no longer applies to
  Antigravity: consumeOAuthCallback returns early for the provider, and
  the antigravity-specific postMessage/BroadcastChannel completion
  branches are removed (the generic handoff keeps working for every
  other provider). The now-dead antigravityCallback() helper and the
  oauthLoopbackCallbackURL import are removed.

## Before / after — authorize URL parameter set

- Before: client_id, redirect_uri=<dashboard origin>/callback (or
  client-supplied), response_type, scope, access_type, prompt, state.
- After: client_id, redirect_uri=https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback,
  response_type, scope (same order), access_type, prompt, state,
  code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256.

## Mechanical test updates

- internal/handlers/oauth/antigravity_test.go: authorize assertions now
  pin the fixed Google redirect (the request still passes a legacy
  ?redirect_uri= to prove it is ignored), the full 7-scope agy list
  (the old expectation predated the aicode/openid alignment), prompt
  and PKCE parameters; TestGetAntigravityRedirectURI deleted with the
  helper; exchange error cases replace the redirect-uri cases with
  missing/unknown state; the success test authorizes first and its mock
  token endpoint now requires the fixed redirect, a verifier matching
  the authorize challenge, and no client_secret — and the re-exchange
  leg mints a fresh authorize round because verifiers are single-use.
  (File sits behind the sqlite_legacy tag; its package test build is
  broken at HEAD by freebuff_test.go's db.OpenDatabase reference —
  pre-existing, identical before and after this fragment.)
- web/src/api/client.test.ts: the Antigravity contract test now expects
  GET /api/oauth/antigravity/authorize with no query and an exchange
  body of exactly {code, state}.

## Deliberately unchanged

- getAntigravityOAuthConfig still surfaces the configured client secret
  to the package; the sign-in exchange simply no longer sends it.
  Refresh/exchange code paths outside this handler (fragment 970) keep
  their own behavior.
- The risk-notice gate before the Antigravity modal, the popup window
  itself, and cleanAuthCode's paste tolerance.

## [v1.9.22] - 2026-11-07

# CodeBuddy leftovers: combo-picker credit pill, costAware editor toggle, CN X-Domain verdict

Closes the three deferrals fragment 976 recorded.

## (a) Credit pill in the combo picker

Phase 2 left the picker without the credit pill because the picker builds
its model list from the static `web/src/lib/models.ts` bundle, and copying
credit values there would create a second home for numbers that belong to
the one table in `internal/providers/codebuddy_catalog.go`. The pill now
reads the values from the server instead:

- `pickerExtras.ts` `loadPickerExtras` fetches `GET /api/models/caps` —
  the endpoint fragment 976 already wired `credit` into — for exactly the
  three providers whose caps can carry a price (`codebuddy-cn`,
  `codebuddy-intl`, `workbuddy`, exported as `CREDIT_CAPS_PROVIDERS`).
  Fetching caps for every catalog provider would be ~100 requests per
  picker open for data only these three have. Each fetch fails soft like
  the other extras, and the results land in
  `ResolvedPickerExtras.modelCaps`, keyed `"<provider>/<model>"`.
  `PickerExtrasSource.getModelCaps` is optional so existing test doubles
  keep working.
- `pickerData.ts` threads the map through: `PickerExtras.modelCaps`,
  `PickerModel.credit` / `PickerModel.free` (flattened scalars, like the
  caps booleans, so pill props compare by value), attached by
  `creditFields()` at all three catalog push sites (bundle models,
  customs, aliases). Node groups carry no credit — the family providers
  are catalog providers, not nodes.
- `ModelPill.svelte` renders the same two forms as the provider detail
  grid (`ProviderDetailView.svelte`): a FREE badge when the server marks
  the model free, otherwise `x{n.toFixed(2)}` with the "Credits per
  request" tooltip. On the selected (brand-filled) pill the badge/pill
  switches to a white-on-brand variant to stay readable.

The static bundle stays free of credit values; the backend table remains
the only source.

## (b) costAware toggle in the combo editor

The backend half shipped in fragment 976 (`db.ComboStrategy.CostAware`,

`chat.OrderByCredit`); only the editor control was missing. It now sits

# 980 — Egress-consistency auditing in the routing log

## Problem

The per-request lines that land in `logs/routing.log` already named
the connection (`conn=…`) and the egress path's label (`egress=…`, a
pool name or "direct") — but never the address the request actually
left from. For a rotating pool the label is stable while the address
changes underneath it, and a provider that rate-limits or blocks by IP
cannot be diagnosed from a label. An account whose path silently moved
to a different egress mid-day — exactly the drift the anti-suspend work
hunts — was invisible in the log.

## What was built

- `internal/handlers/chat/egress_ip.go` — the tracker. Each chat-lane
  log entry for a connection now also carries:
  - `egress_ip` — the last-known egress IPv4 of the connection's path,
    discovered by an echo lookup THROUGH the connection's own client
    (`getClientForConnection`: same pool/proxy/relay/direct transport
    the request itself used), against the same echo targets the
    dashboard's exit-node probe uses (v4.ident.me,
    whatismyip.akamai.com, ipv4.icanhazip.com).
  - `egress_changed` — `old->new`, present only when this connection's
    path IP differs from the one its previous entry carried.
- Freshness without blocking: lookups are cached per path for 10
  minutes and refreshed in a background goroutine (single-flight per
  path; a failed lookup keeps the last-known IP and retries after 1
  minute). The request path only reads the cached value — it never
  waits on an echo. A path's first-ever entry therefore carries no
  `egress_ip` yet; the value appears from the next entry on.
- Path identity (the cache key) is credential-free: the resolved
  pool's id (`pool:<id>`), a relay's host (`relay:<host>`), a short
  SHA-256 prefix of a legacy proxy target (`proxy:<hash>` — a proxy
  URL can carry credentials and is never used raw), or `direct`.
- Both caches are in-memory only (deliberate): a restart forgets the
  previous per-connection IPs, so the first entry after a boot carries
  no `egress_changed` marker — there is nothing honest to compare
  against.
- Hook points (`internal/handlers/chat/fallback.go`): the success
  usage record and both failure records (upstream failure and the
  proxy-blocked early return) — the same entries that already carried
  `egress=`. The snapshot is taken once per attempt, so sibling lines
  of one attempt agree and a change is marked once, on the attempt
  that observed it. Emission is via `UsageLogInfo.ConnIdentityKV`
  (`internal/handlers/shared/types.go`: new `EgressIP` /
  `EgressChanged` fields), which the `[usage]` line and the fallback
  failure lines already print. Scope: the chat lane — the media lanes
  build their own usage records and do not carry the fields.

## Verification

- Temporary in-package probe (stub transports + a local stub HTTP
  proxy; deleted after the run, suite not run): PASS —
  - direct path: first fill returns immediately with no IP (proves the
    request path never blocks on the echo); after the background
    refresh lands, fills carry `egress_ip=203.0.113.7` with no marker;
  - forced change: stub answer flipped and TTL lapsed → the next fill
    carries `egress_ip=203.0.113.9` and
    `egress_changed=203.0.113.7->203.0.113.9`; `ConnIdentityKV` emits
    both keys;
  - proxied path: echo travelled through the connection's own proxy
    (stub proxy answering every absolute-URI GET), path key is
    `proxy:<hash>`, never the raw URL.
- Boot smoke (staging PG, scratch DB, dropped after): gateway boots
  on the new binary, `/api/version` answers, and
  `<DATA_DIR>/logs/routing.log` is created and written.
- `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean on internal/handlers/chat and
  internal/handlers/shared.

# 979 — Scheduled generation probe for idle Antigravity accounts

## Problem

Fragment 973's ToS-disable detection is traffic-driven: the chat lane
classifies generation responses as they pass. An account Google
disabled while it sat idle produces no generation responses, so the
disable stays invisible until the account's next real request draws the
verdict — mid-rotation, in front of a user.

## What was built

- `internal/schedule/idleprobe.go` — the prober. On a 1-minute tick
  (first sweep 15s after boot) it lists Antigravity connections and
  probes each due one with ONE tiny generation request through the
  existing in-process probe lane, `ChatHandler.PingConnection`
  (connection pinned, probe context) — the same lane the quota
  auto-ping uses, i.e. real credential resolution, OAuth refresh,
  proxy-pool binding and executor. No HTTP self-call and no new probe
  implementation: the test-model route's decisive surface IS the
  generation path, and this is it, in-process. The loadCodeAssist
  connection probe is deliberately NOT used (it answers for terminated
  accounts).
- The response flows through the chat lane's existing classification
  untouched: a ToS 403 disables the account exactly as live traffic
  would (973), a 429 parks it as live traffic would, a transport
  failure changes nothing. Fail-open: a failed probe is logged and
  dropped; the prober itself writes no account state, ever.
- Probe shape: model `gemini-3.8-flash-low` (cheapest broadly-entitled
  flash lane; the disable verdict is account-shaped, not model-shaped),
  prompt "hi", max_tokens 1 — the auto-ping body shape.
- Guardrails: concurrency 1 (sequential sweep); due list shuffled with
  a jittered 3–13s pause between probes; at most 8 probes per tick;
  per-account minimum interval enforced from an in-memory last-probe
  map (an attempt counts, so a dead-egress account is not re-probed
  every tick). Disabled accounts are never dialed: a connection is
  skipped when it is inactive OR carries the stored disabled verdict
  (data.status / data.testStatus == "disabled", the
  DisableConnectionWithReason marker) — the second check covers the
  resurrection shape (marker intact on an active row) where isActive
  alone would let a probe through. Idle is measured from the
  connection's lastUsedAt stamp (creation time for never-used rows).
- `internal/app/server.go` — `startIdleProbe` wired beside the
  auto-ping scheduler, bound to the shutdown context.

## Settings (one home)

All in `providerStrategies.<provider>` (`internal/db/settings.go`),
resolved per sweep by `Repo.IdleProbeConfigFor`
(`internal/db/accounts_idleprobe.go`), following fragment 974's
derived-default pattern:

- `idleProbeEnabled` — unset = derived default (enabled for
  antigravity, off elsewhere); explicit false turns the prober off.
- `idleProbeThresholdSec` — unset or non-positive = 6 hours.
- `idleProbeIntervalSec` — unset or non-positive = 1 hour.

Only antigravity is in the prober's scope even when another provider's
strategy enables it: the disable blindness being closed is
Antigravity's, and no other provider's verdicts feed a disable path.

## Quota cost, honestly

Each probe is one real generation call against the account's own quota
("hi", one output token, cheapest flash lane). With the defaults, a
permanently idle account is probed ~4 times a day; an account with any
real traffic is probed rarely or never, because traffic keeps
resetting its idle clock. This is a deliberate trade: a handful of
one-token generations per idle account per day, in exchange for
learning about a ToS disable on a background tick instead of from a
failed user request.

## Found and fixed on the way (latent bug, shipped code)

`applyProviderStrategies` (`internal/db/settings_parse_maps.go`)
rebuilds every ProviderStrategy field-by-field and never carried the
pointer knobs — fragment 974's `cooldownJitterSec` was silently dropped
on the parse path, so its EXPLICIT setting has been dead since v1.9.20
(only the derived default ever applied). The parse now carries
`cooldownJitterSec` plus the three new idle-probe fields verbatim
(presence-checked, since explicit 0/false is a decision for these
knobs). Without this fix the settings above could not have been read
at all.

## Verification (boot smoke, staging PG, scratch DB — dropped after)

Seeded three Antigravity connections (fake credentials): A = active,
idle 24h; B = active but carrying the stored disabled marker; C =
inactive, idle 24h.

- Phase A, `idleProbeThresholdSec=999999999` in providerStrategies:
  two sweeps, ZERO probe/skip lines — the settings home governs.
- Phase B, threshold flipped to 60 (settings row only, no restart):
  the next tick logged `skipping stored-disabled connection` for B and
  `probing idle connection` for A — and nothing for C. B's row was
  byte-unchanged afterwards (updatedAt still the seed instant, no
  lastError): never dialed. A's probe travelled the lane and its
  existing classification disabled the account (the fake credential
  resolves to no project ID — the lane's own disable verdict, recorded
  with lastError), proving end-to-end that a probe verdict lands in
  the same disable path as live traffic. With real credentials the
  same dispatch draws the upstream's actual generation verdict.
- `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean on internal/db,
  internal/schedule, internal/app.
