## [v1.9.21] - 2026-11-07

# 977 — CodeBuddy family Phase 3 (final): bulk-JWT UI, intl identity backfill, userinfo probes, error-classification alignment, SSE finish_reason repair

Phase 3 of closing the CodeBuddy-family gaps (audit CB #18–#26, WB #9,
#10, #14–#19; CB #8). Builds on Phase 1 (fragment 975) and Phase 2
(fragment 976). JS sources are the behavioral spec; Go ports contracts,
not code.

## 1. Bulk JWT UI (CB #24, WB #9)

The route POST /api/oauth/{provider}/bulk-jwt existed with no frontend.
Now it has the dashboard surface upstream has:

- New `web/src/components/connections/BulkImportJwtModal.svelte`
  (upstream BulkImportJwtModal.js, in this codebase's modal idiom):
  paste box, the accepted formats, and the per-import result exactly as
  upstream renders it — "✓ N added · ⊘ N duplicates skipped · ✗ N
  failed" plus the per-failed-item "[index] error" list. Entries with
  both tokens become OAuth connections with auto-refresh (server-side
  behavior, unchanged).
- `ProviderDetailView.svelte`: a "Bulk Add" button (playlist_add) in
  the Connections toolbar, gated to the three family providers via
  `supportsJwtBulkImport` (upstream ConnectionsSection gating), and the
  modal mounted alongside the other connection modals; a successful
  import refreshes the list.
- `web/src/api/client.ts`: `api.bulkImportJwt(providerId, text)` +
  `BulkJwtImportResult` / `BulkJwtImportEntry` types.
- Add-connection bulk tab (upstream AddApiKeyModal behavior): for the
  family providers a JSON-shaped paste now routes to bulk-jwt instead
  of the per-key plan — `isJsonAccountPayload` → POST bulk-jwt and
  surface {success, failed, skipped}; JSON-shaped but token-less →
  "This JSON has no accessToken/refreshToken. Check the account export
  shape." The detectors are ported into `web/src/lib/bulk-add.ts`
  (bulkAdd.js), including the concatenated-pretty-JSON token-field
  fallback; plain `name|token` lines still take the per-key plan.

## 2. Intl identity backfill (CB #25)

Upstream's run-once `backfillCodeBuddyIntlIdentity`
(src/lib/oauth/providers/index.js), called from GET /api/providers and
GET /api/providers/client, repairs codebuddy-intl oauth rows that hold
an access token but no email/displayName, or still carry a generic
"Account N" name — the identity is recovered from the stored JWT.

- Hook: `DashboardHandler.backfillCodebuddyIntlIdentity`, called at the
  top of `HandleGetProvidersClient` — the handler serving those exact
  two routes (`internal/handlers/dashboard/codebuddy_intl_backfill.go`).
  This is the repo's lazy-repair idiom (cf. fragment 972's identity pin
  backfill on dashboard reads).
- Run-once per process behind a mutex, with upstream's reset-on-failure
  semantics: a pass that cannot read or write stays pending and the
  next list call retries it. A failed pass never fails the list call.
- Extraction precedence matches the family's device-save helpers
  (fragment 975): email → preferred_username → sub; displayName → name
  claim → given+family → email local part. Rename target is
  email || displayName, only for /^Account \d+$/ names.
- Write: `db.Repo.SetConnectionCodebuddyIntlIdentity` fills only empty
  fields (data.email, data.displayName, the email column, optionally
  the name) in one UPDATE — so the pass is idempotent by construction:
  rows already carrying identity are never in the patch set, and a
  second pass finds nothing to do. WorkBuddy and CN have no upstream
  backfill; none was invented.

## 3. Connection verification probes (CB #26, WB #10)

Upstream testUtils.js probes codebuddy-intl and workbuddy at the
Keycloak userinfo endpoint of the realm the token's `iss` claim names
(fallback realms www.codebuddy.ai / www.workbuddy.ai), marked
refreshable. Go's probe table had intl as a {tokenExists:true} stub and
workbuddy missing entirely.

- `connection_probe.go`: both providers now carry a real config —
  buildURL deriving `<iss>/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo`, GET,
  Bearer, `refreshable: true` — so they ride the file's established
  machinery (connection proxy, refresh-on-401 with the family's real
  refreshers from fragment 975, token persistence).
- The URL builder lives in `connection_probe_codebuddy.go`: `iss` is
  used only when it starts with https:// (trailing slash trimmed),
  exactly upstream's guard.
- CN stays {tokenExists:true} — upstream has no userinfo probe for it.
- ToS-disabled rows stay protected by fragment 973's guard: the probe
  still never dials for them.

## 4. Error classification alignment (CB #18–#23, WB #14–#19)

The old Go readings sentenced accounts on bare text: "restricted" /
"unusual activity" → 7 days at ANY status for the family, 14018 → a
generic 2 minutes, "request illegal" → an intl-only backoff. All
replaced by upstream's gated verdicts. New classifier fields carry what
a substring rule cannot: `ErrorRule.Exhausted / ModelScoped /
RequestLevel` and `ErrorClassification.Exhausted / ModelScoped`.

### Gated verdicts (new `internal/providers/errorclassify_codebuddy.go`)

Consulted before ErrorRules, where upstream puts them:

- **11140** (checkFallbackError's guard, code-gated — upstream gates on
  the code literal, which only the family emits): HTTP 403 + code 11140
  + restriction wording (WB_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION_RE) → **2h, account
  lock, exhausted**. Bare 11140 → **5 min, account lock, NOT
  exhausted**. A safety wording in the body vetoes the guard, and the
  request-level safety rules decide instead. The classifier receives
  the extracted error text, whose "(code 11140)" suffix (and the raw
  JSON body shape) both match WB_11140_CODE_RE.
- **Family 429 sentences** (markAccountUnavailable's 429 block,
  provider-gated, applied in upstream's order — a later check may
  replace an earlier verdict):
  - "model busy" text or a bare 14003 token → **model-scoped 5s**,
    flat, backoff level reset to 0.
  - Throttle wording (too many requests | rate.?limit exceeded | rate
    limited | usage exceeds frequency limit) with NO quota wording →
    **model-scoped 2 min**, never exhausted.
  - "credits exhausted" / "insufficient credits" text or a bare 14018
    token → **account-wide, exhausted, 7 days** (the direct path).
    Upstream keys on the wording; the bare code is its constant
    companion on the wire, so either claims the verdict.

### Rule-table changes (`errorclassify.go`)

- **Generic credit family** → upstream ERROR_RULES exactly: the 16
  texts (insufficient_user_quota, 预扣费额度失败, 用户剩余额度,
  用户额度不足, "user's credit limit is insufficient", "quota is
  running low", credits exhausted, insufficient credits, insufficient
  balance, out of credits, quota reached, quota exhausted,
  insufficient_quota, insufficient quota, exceeded your current quota,
  monthly quota exceeded) → **30 days, exhausted** (new
  cooldownMonthlyExhausted), placed before the older 1-hour quota
  spellings so the request path's verdict wins on overlapping texts.
  The 1-hour spellings ERROR_RULES does not carry (insufficient credit
  singular, credit exhausted singular, no remaining credits, quota
  exceeded, monthly limit, frequency limit, payment required, free
  allowance, credit balance is too low) are unchanged.
- **11158** → one rule: status 400 only, **cooldown 0, model-scoped**
  (the plan gate: skip the member/model, the account stays healthy).
  The duplicated 2-minute copies are gone.
- **Request-level rules, global** (upstream ERROR_RULES):
  "did not pass the safety review", "safety review", "request illegal",
  "content filter" → no fallback, no lock, no cooldown — for
  codebuddy-cn and workbuddy too (WB #19). "conversation id missing"
  travels with them: the current upstream ERROR_RULES carries no entry
  for it (verified by grep), and its old intl-only backoff reading
  parked accounts over a request fault, so it takes the same
  request-level verdict as its sibling instead of a distinct invented
  one.
- Deleted: all bare-text family restriction rules (7d at any status),
  the generic "unusual activity"/"restricted" 7d+30min copies, the
  family "11140" substring rules, the generic 14018 2-minute rules,
  and the duplicated rule blocks.

### Consumers

- **Exhausted representation** — no new flag: Go's status model already
  derives `quota_exhausted` from the stored lastError text
  (`EffectiveStatusWithError` via `LooksLikeQuotaExhausted`), checked
  before the stale-marker recovery so a spent account stays exhausted
  after its timer lapses. `connection_status.go` itself needed no edit;
  the vocabulary in `errorclassify.go` gained the two family markers
  whose texts carry no credit wording — "14018" and "restricted due to
  unusual activity" — both Tencent-only strings.
- `cooldownSecForClassification` (retry_after.go): an Exhausted
  verdict now rides the banned class's unclamped path (a 7d/30d
  sentence must not be cut to the 72h reset ceiling or replaced by a
  429's Retry-After), and a ModelScoped verdict returns the
  classifier's exact duration (the flat 5s busy sentence must not be
  replaced by a reset reading).
- Scope: both failover loops (fallback.go, combo.go) now honor
  `cls.ModelScoped` ahead of the isModelScopedError text guess — the
  gated busy/throttle bodies carry no quota text for the guess to see,
  and parking the account for them was the bug being fixed.
- fallback.go: a `!ShouldFallback` classification now excludes the
  connection for the turn with NO lock writes, mirroring the combo
  path's standing guard (request-level refusals at retryable statuses
  previously still wrote account state).
- **Combo member attempt cap** (combo.go, both member loops):
  `comboMemberAttemptCap` returns 1 for codebuddy-cn / codebuddy-intl /
  workbuddy (upstream COMBO_MEMBER_ACCOUNT_ATTEMPTS_BY_PROVIDER — the
  burst is what the vendor's risk control answers with 11140) and the
  standing 10 for everyone else. Only attempts that actually reach the
  upstream count; a connection skipped as already-locked was never
  dialled and does not spend the budget.

## 5. Executor SSE repair (CB #8)

Upstream's streaming passthrough (open-sse/utils/stream.js) rewrites
CodeBuddy's `finish_reason: ""` to null on chunks and forwards only
the first [DONE]. Go now does the same on the family's streaming path
only: `codebuddySSENormalizer` (`internal/proxy/executor/
codebuddy_sse.go`) wraps the stall reader at forwardCodebuddy's single
stream call site — all three brands, one place — and transforms line
by line (never buffering the stream): a data chunk whose choices carry
an empty finish_reason is re-serialized with null; every other line,
including the terminal chunk, passes through byte-identical; duplicate
`data: [DONE]` lines are dropped after the first. The shared
execSSEStream/sseStream and every other provider's stream are
untouched.

## Deliberate non-changes

- **CB #7 X-Domain**: UNVERIFIED which value the upstream accepts —
  both sides left exactly as they are.
- **CB #9 conversation-UUID shape**: Go keeps its session-derived
  conversation ids; WorkBuddy already uses fresh ids per JS.

- **WorkBuddy is a registered provider** (CodeBuddy-family gap audit WB #1–#4). Registry entry mirroring `open-sse/providers/registry/workbuddy.js`: id `workbuddy`, alias `wb`, priority 90, authModes [oauth, apikey], passthroughModels, Tencent-blue `smart_toy` identity, signup invite URL. The dashboard catalog branch (`isCodebuddyFamily`) now includes `workbuddy`/`wb`, resolving through the canonical id to that list. Frontend: `web/src/lib/models.ts` gains the `wb` alias + model list, and `ProviderDetailView` treats `workbuddy` as a device-OAuth provider; the provider catalog itself is API-driven from the Go registry, so the card appears with no further UI wiring.
- **WorkBuddy capabilities and thinking levels.** The 12 per-model entries from `open-sse/providers/capabilities.js` (including the GLM vision:false guard — the server drops images while claiming support) plus the registry layer-0 declarations for the presets and newer ids, merged into `providerCapabilities["workbuddy"]` because Go has no separate registry-caps layer; without the preset rows the capabilities gate in `GetThinkingLevels` would swallow the preset patterns. The 7 provider-qualified thinking patterns from `open-sse/providers/thinkingLevels.js` are ported with JS placement: presets (`fast`/`balanced` = medium, `primary` = high) and `deepseek-v4*` above the unqualified glob, `glm-5.3*`/`glm-5.2`/`hy3*` with the per-model block. Preset levels verified live in-process: fast-model → [medium], glm-5.2 → [high xhigh], hy3 → [low high], deepseek-v4.1-flash → [low high xhigh].
- **WorkBuddy executor** (WB #5, the audit BLOCKER). `ForwardWorkbuddy` is a thin flavor of the shared CodeBuddy forward — the way upstream's `workbuddy.js` executor extends the CodeBuddy executor — reusing force-stream, the reasoning mirror, the prompt merge (with the leading identity swapped to "You are WorkBuddy."), and 6004 parsing. Its header builder starts from the CodeBuddy set and then strips the CodeBuddy CLI/Stainless identity (`X-Stainless-*`, `X-App`, `X-Private-Data`, `X-CodeBuddy-Request`; channel verification error 11128), sets the mandatory `WorkBuddy/5.5.6` client identity (error 10085 without it) with `X-IDE-Type`/`X-IDE-Name` = WorkBuddy and `X-Agent-Type: main`, mints fresh channel/conversation ids per request, honors the connection's `domain` override, and sets `X-User-Id` from the connection JWT with upstream's claim precedence (user_id → userId → uid → sub). Verified against a local fake upstream: identity headers exact, stripped headers absent, conversation ids differ across calls, request id equals message id, stream forced, WorkBuddy prompt injected. The existing `ck_` API-key branch behavior is preserved (the executor's Go-only extra).
- **CodeBuddy-family request pacing** (CB #10). Upstream paces all three brands at 120 req/min through a leaky bucket on request starts (`open-sse/utils/providerRateLimiter.js`, applied by the shared executor base — codebuddy-cn, codebuddy-intl, and workbuddy alike). `internal/proxy/executor/codebuddy_pacing.go` implements the same semantics in-process: 500 ms slot interval per provider, at most 12 waiting, fail-open when the queue is full or the wait would exceed 2 s, context-aware sleep. Upstream's Valkey-backed distributed variant is not ported — this gateway is a single process, so the in-memory bucket is the whole mechanism.
- **Real CodeBuddy-family token refreshers** (CB #11, WB #6). New `internal/proxy/oauth/codebuddy.go` registers dedicated refreshers for `codebuddy-cn`, `codebuddy-intl`, and `workbuddy` implementing the upstream contract (`open-sse/services/tokenRefresh/providers.js`): POST `{host}/v2/plugin/auth/token/refresh` with an empty JSON body and the refresh token in the `X-Refresh-Token` header, per-brand User-Agent (`CLI/2.63.2 CodeBuddy/2.63.2` / `IDE/2.63.2 CodeBuddy/2.63.2` / `IDE/2.63.2 WorkBuddy/2.63.2`), `X-Domain`, `X-Auth-Refresh-Source: plugin`, `X-Product: SaaS`. Hosts: CN → copilot.tencent.com, Intl → www.codebuddy.ai, WorkBuddy → www.workbuddy.ai. A rotated refresh token is persisted via the standard connection update; when the response carries none, the stored token is carried through. Because the refreshers register from `init()`, `RegisterAll` skips these providers, so the generic env-gated form-POST path can never fire for the family; the `KnownOAuthConfigs` entries now document the correct per-brand hosts (intl previously pointed at the CN host `copilot.tencent.com`) and a `workbuddy` entry was added.
- **Device-save identity merge for the family** (CB #13/#14, WB #7/#8). The dedicated device flow now supports `workbuddy` end to end (provider list, start, poll — the dynamic dispatch already had it). `saveDeviceConnection` merges a family re-login by provider + email (upstream `connectionsRepo.js` behavior): when an email is known, the existing active row's id is reused so a rotated token updates the row instead of creating a credential-hash duplicate; the hash identity remains the fallback when no email can be determined. Polls now carry `expires_in` → `expiresAt` for all three providers, defaulting to 86400 when absent (upstream `mapTokens`), and capture displayName from the JWT — intl via the name/given/family/local-part extraction, WorkBuddy as the account email per its `mapTokens` — persisted alongside the email. CN stays email-only, as upstream.

## [v1.9.20] - 2026-11-06

## Antigravity rotation pacing — mechanism C IMPLEMENTED (A and B declined)

Status: **C implemented** (2026-11-06, uncommitted); A and B remain
design only. Ordered on the anti-suspend track (2026-11-06) after
fragment 973: the goal is to remove the machine-like shape of pool
rotation, grounded in what the code does today — every behavioral
claim below is cited, and every number is labelled **DERIVED** (read
from observed quota/upstream data or an existing in-repo precedent)
or **PROPOSAL** (a value for the operator to pick; nothing in the
data picks it for us). The implementation record at the end of this
fragment states what actually shipped, with its parameters and
verification evidence.

### Current behavior (survey, 2026-11-06, main @ 94f17710 + fragment 973)

**Selection.** `ChatHandler.getBestConnectionWithContext`
(`internal/handlers/chat/connections.go`) loads the active rows only
(`Repo.GetProviderConnections(provider, true)` — `isActive = 1`;
`internal/db/connections.go`, order: priority ASC, NULLs last, then
`updatedAt DESC`), filters strict model assignment and per-model
eligibility, drops rows parked by `connectionModelBlocked` (per-model
lock or the in-memory quota cache) and rows whose
`db.ConnectionBlockedUntil` (the earlier of `rateLimitedUntil` /
`oauthLockedUntil`) is in the future, then takes the **first** survivor
of the strategy-ordered list. Order comes from
`applyConnectionStrategy` (`connections.go`): `round-robin`/`sticky` →
`selectByRecency` (persistent LRU with a consecutive-use sticky limit,
stamped via the row's `lastUsedAt`/`consecutiveUseCount`); `random` → a
random rotation; anything else — including **no strategy configured** —
keeps DB priority order, i.e. **fill-first: the top account absorbs
everything until it errors**. Strategy source is
`connRotationStrategy` (per-provider `settings.ProviderStrategies`,
falling back to the global fallback strategy unless it is `fill-first`).
Session affinity (affinity-eligible strategies only) pins a session to
one account and forces `StickyLimit = 1` for new sessions; the binding
is evicted on 429/401/403. A client-pinned connection is honored only
when eligible (`pinnedConnectionIneligible`); probes bypass cooldowns
and locks but never a disabled row.

**Account-state vocabulary** (all in the `providerConnections.data`
blob unless noted): `isActive` (column; 0 = disabled — fragment 973's
terminal state), `status`/`testStatus`, `lastError {status, message,
timestamp[, model, source]}`, `rateLimitedUntil` (account-scoped quota
cooldown), `backoffLevel`, `modelLock_<model>` timestamps (per-model
parks; Antigravity models canonicalized, e.g. the tiered flash pool),
`oauthLockedUntil` + `oauthFailureCount` (rejected-grant park),
`verificationUrl`, the `quotas` snapshot (last dashboard usage fetch;
deleted by status resets), `providerSpecificData.antigravityIdentity`
(fragment 972's pin), plus the row columns `priority`, `lastUsedAt`,
`consecutiveUseCount`.

**Failover on 429 QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, step by step.**
`handleAccountFallback` (`internal/handlers/chat/fallback.go`) walks
the strategy-ordered candidate list, one attempt per account,
**with no delay or jitter between hops** — hops are bounded only by
pool size. Each failure is classified by
`providers.ClassifyErrorForProvider` (`internal/providers/errorclassify.go`)
and turned into parked seconds by `cooldownSecForClassification`
(`internal/handlers/chat/retry_after.go`): a 429's own announced wait
wins (Retry-After header, `google.rpc.RetryInfo` `retryDelay`,
`quotaResetDelay`, "Resets in X"), clamped to `maxResetCooldown` = 72h;
quota-worded bodies take the fixed `QuotaExhaustedCooldownMs` = 1h;
a bare 429 takes exponential backoff, 2s base doubling to a 5min cap
(`GetQuotaCooldown`, backoff level persisted, max level 15). The writes
on the exhausted account (`Repo` in `internal/db/accounts.go`):
`LockConnectionModel` on the canonical **and** raw model keys, always;
then, if the error is not model-scoped (`isModelScopedError`),
`LockConnectionRateLimit` sets `rateLimitedUntil = now + cooldown` —
model-scoped errors only `RecordConnectionScopedError` and leave the
account selectable for other models. ToS-shaped 403s disable instead
(fragment 973). A later success clears locks, cooldown and backoff in
one guarded statement (`ClearConnectionSuccessState`). **Re-eligibility
is purely the stored timestamp passing** — nothing else clears a
cooldown early except a success on that account or an operator reset
endpoint. In parallel, the native Antigravity path
(`internal/handlers/chat/gemini_handler.go`) feeds 409/429s to
`HandleAntigravityQuotaError` (`internal/handlers/chat/antigravity_quota.go`),
which refreshes live quota (30s minimum refresh interval) and blocks
the model in the **in-memory** quota cache until the upstream's own
`resetAt`; a strike-breaker adds a 15min cache block after 3
marker-carrying 429s in 60s against an optimistic quota reading.
Combos (`handleComboFallbackWithVisited`,
`internal/handlers/chat/combo.go`) run the same per-member lock writes
and add the system's **only** inter-attempt delay: after a fully failed
pass, one repeat pass waits the earliest Retry-After — capped at 2s
when a 429 was involved, 8s otherwise — plus 100–400ms jitter
(`passRetry.wait` / `addRetryJitter` in `retry_after.go`). If every
account is in cooldown and the operator enabled force-fallback, the
soonest-to-reset account is served anyway
(`forceMinCooldownConnection`).

**Pacing-like machinery that already exists** (build on it, don't
duplicate): the cooldown/backoff system above; the OAuth rejection
park (5min doubling to 24h, `internal/db/accounts_oauth_lock.go`);
the fragment-968 background-refresh de-synchronisation (5min tick,
shuffled due order, accounts spaced 1.5s — 12s for sensitive providers
incl. Google — plus 0–50% jitter, `internal/proxy/oauth/background.go`);
the 55s usage cache and the 30s quota-refresh floor (background-call
pressure, not generation pacing); the strike-breaker; the seat attempt
budget (`SeatAttemptBudgetMs`, bounds attempt *duration*, not rate).

**What a cap could be measured against.** There is **no maintained
per-account request counter**. What exists: `usageHistory` rows per
served request (`Repo.InsertUsageHistory`, `internal/db/usage.go` —
timestamp, provider, model, connectionId, status, tokens), from which
per-account counts over any window are one aggregation away; the
per-request in-memory `FallbackAttemptRecorder` (attempt outcomes,
dies with the request); and the routing log
(`<dataDir>/logs/routing.log`, mirrored at boot in
`internal/app/server.go`) — observability, not a meter. The selection
hot path reads only the connection row plus in-memory caches, and
AGENTS.md §4.A/§4.G forbid a per-selection aggregate query on the
1-vCPU target: any cap therefore needs an **in-memory counter**
incremented on the attempt path, bootstrapped from `usageHistory` at
boot, with the DB remaining the audit trail rather than the meter.

### Mechanism A — switch pacing (minimum dwell after an exhaustion event)

- **Mechanics.** When an account-scoped quota lock is written during a
  client turn, record a pool-level `lastSwitchAt` (in memory, per
  provider+model family). The fallback loop — and new turns — may not
  *start* on a different account until `dwell` has elapsed since the
  exhaustion event; a turn that arrives early waits (bounded by the
  seat budget) or returns the 429 with `Retry-After` = remaining dwell.
  Today this hop costs 0ms (`handleAccountFallback`), which is the
  single most machine-like observable in the system: account B's first
  request lands in the same millisecond account A's quota died.
- **Parameters (all PROPOSAL).** `switchDwell` ∈ {5s, 15s, 30s, 60s};
  scope: quota-class locks only (never transient 5xx/auth parks);
  optional escalation ×2 per consecutive pool-wide exhaustion round,
  capped ×8. No value is derivable from quota data — the upstream
  announces resets, not switch etiquette.
- **Cost.** Added latency on exactly the turns that already failed
  once; zero cost on healthy turns. No failed requests added (the turn
  either waits or returns the same 429 it returns today).
- **Evidence.** For: the zero-delay hop is a proven fact of the current
  code, and dwell directly removes it. Against: Google observes
  per-account traffic, not the router's internal hop timing — the
  dwell is only visible as the gap between A's last request and B's
  first, and only under sustained load; under sporadic load it is
  inert. It shapes bursts, it does not reduce total per-account load.

### Mechanism B — per-account request pacing

- **B1, minimum interval.** A per-connection in-memory leaky bucket:
  generation attempts on one account start at least `minInterval`
  apart; a request that arrives early **waits** (spilling to the next
  account would defeat the purpose — that *is* rotation). Parameters
  (PROPOSAL): `minInterval` ∈ {0 (off), 500ms, 1s, 2s}. Cost: latency
  under concurrency, head-of-line blocking on a hot account. Evidence:
  weakest of the three — a real `agy` client can legitimately burst,
  and no observed Google threshold sits between the quota itself and
  human typing speed. Included for completeness, not recommended.
- **B2, rolling caps.** Per-connection counters (in-memory, per §
  "measured against" above): at `capHour` requests in a rolling hour
  or `capDay` in a rolling day, the account is treated as in-cooldown
  until the window slides. Parameters (PROPOSAL): `capHour` ∈ {60,
  120, 300}, `capDay` ∈ {500, 1000, 2000}. The only DERIVED anchor is
  negative: Antigravity's own limits are per-model remaining-% with
  an upstream `resetAt` plus weekly/session family windows (the quota
  cache in `antigravity_quota.go`) — Google already caps by quota, so
  a count cap is a blunter behavioral proxy ("look like one person's
  CLI"), not a quota-derived number, and it must be presented as such.
  Cost: stranded quota (an account parked by our cap while Google
  would still serve it), new counter state with boot reconciliation,
  and client-visible 429s whenever the whole pool is capped.

### Mechanism C — jittered re-eligibility

- **Mechanics.** A cooldown's stored expiry stays the floor, but the
  account becomes selectable at `expiry + rand(0, jitterWindow)`,
  drawn once per lock event (stored alongside the lock, or derived
  deterministically from connection id + expiry so no extra write is
  needed). Applies to `rateLimitedUntil`, per-model locks, and the
  in-memory quota-cache blocks alike.
- **Parameters.** `jitterWindow` ∈ {30s, 2min, 5min} or 10% of the
  cooldown capped at 5min — PROPOSAL values, but the *shape* is
  DERIVED from two in-repo precedents: fragment 968 already jitters
  background refresh by +0–50% for exactly this reason ("fixed spacing
  marches the whole fleet in lockstep, which is itself a detectable
  pattern", `internal/proxy/oauth/background.go`), and combo retries
  already add 100–400ms jitter (`retry_after.go`).
- **Cost.** Near zero: a bounded delay at a moment the account was
  unusable anyway; no request fails that wouldn't have. One
  interaction to respect in implementation: force-fallback reads the
  stored `until` to pick the soonest account — jitter must apply
  consistently there, or the operator's escape hatch silently bypasses
  it (acceptable if deliberate; must not be accidental).
- **Evidence.** For: pool-wide exhaustion is common (one workload
  drains accounts together), so today the whole pool re-enters at the
  exact upstream-announced reset instant — synchronized re-entry is
  both a visible pattern and self-defeating (the herd re-exhausts
  instantly). Against: none observed; the mechanism only ever delays
  eligibility that does not exist yet.

### Recommendation

Implement **C first, then A at the smallest dwell (5–15s)**, and defer
B entirely until there is evidence a per-account rate (not the quota
itself) is what Google reacts to: C removes the synchronized re-entry
pattern at ~zero cost using a jitter shape the codebase already
endorses, A removes the zero-gap switch — the other proven machine
signature — at the price of latency on already-failed turns only,
while B spends real quota and real complexity on thresholds no
observation supports yet. Scope all of it to `antigravity` first
(AGENTS.md §3 provider isolation); the shared selection layer takes it
as per-provider settings next to `ProviderStrategy`, so another
provider can opt in later without a second implementation.

### Non-goals and risks

- **Disabled is terminal for pacing.** Pacing reads only cooldown/lock
  fields; a disabled row (`isActive = 0`) is never in the candidate set
  and no pacing write may set `isActive`, clear `lastError`, or
  otherwise touch fragment 973's state. The precedent guard is
  `ClearConnectionSuccessState`'s C-4 rule: background clears must not
  flip a disabled row back to active.
- **One home, both loops.** Dwell and jitter must live in the shared
  selection/failover layer, not be re-implemented per loop — the
  `cooldownSecForClassification` comment records what happens when
  `fallback.go` and `combo.go` each keep half the semantics. Combo
  second-pass wait behavior stays unchanged.
- **Small pools degrade to no-ops.** With fewer than 2 eligible
  accounts (the staging pool is 4; a 1-account pool is legitimate),
  switch dwell is a no-op (there is no switch), and caps must never
  park the *last* eligible account unless the operator explicitly
  opts into hard caps — default degradation is serve-and-log.
- **Probes stay exempt.** Pinned probes exist to test reachability and
  start quota windows; they already bypass cooldowns and must bypass
  pacing too (they still refuse disabled rows).
- **Hot path stays write-light.** All pacing state is in-memory plus
  the lock writes that already exist; no new per-request DB write and
  no per-selection aggregate query (AGENTS.md §4.A/§4.G).

### Decisions for the operator

| Parameter | Candidates | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `switchDwell` (A) | off / 5s / 15s / 30s / 60s | PROPOSAL |
| dwell escalation | off / ×2 per round, cap ×8 | PROPOSAL |
| `jitterWindow` (C) | 30s / 2min / 5min / 10% of cooldown ≤ 5min | PROPOSAL (shape DERIVED) |
| `minInterval` (B1) | off / 500ms / 1s / 2s | PROPOSAL |
| `capHour` / `capDay` (B2) | 60/120/300 per h; 500/1000/2000 per day | PROPOSAL |
| hard caps on last account | serve-and-log (default) / hard park | PROPOSAL |
| scope | antigravity only (recommended) / all OAuth providers | PROPOSAL |

### Implementation record — mechanism C only (2026-11-06)

**Decision.** Ricki, 2026-11-06 16:17: implement **C only** — "C aja
dulu (jitter kelayakan), tanpa jeda pindah". Mechanism A (switch
dwell) and mechanism B (per-account pacing/caps) are **declined**;
their sections above stay as the design record, unimplemented. This
supersedes the recommendation paragraph, which proposed C + A.

**What shipped.** When an account-scoped cooldown is written for an
antigravity connection, the same UPDATE also stores a re-eligibility
companion — `rateLimitedEligibleAt` beside `rateLimitedUntil`,
`oauthLockedEligibleAt` beside `oauthLockedUntil`
(`internal/db/accounts_pacing.go`). The announced expiry is never
rewritten, so the dashboard keeps rendering the truthful upstream
reset; selection honors the companion. `db.ConnectionBlockedUntil`
now answers with each park's effective instant (the companion when
it is later than its own park, else the announced expiry), which
puts every eligibility consumer on the same jittered instant with
no per-consumer change: the selection filter and the cooldown error
message in `getBestConnectionWithContext`, the session-affinity
bound-connection check (a binding whose account sits in its jitter
tail reads ineligible and is evicted, so the re-pick also honors
jitter), `pinnedConnectionIneligible`, the combo candidate filter,
and force-fallback's soonest-to-reset pick — the escape hatch
compares jittered instants, so it cannot silently bypass the
mechanism. When every account is parked or in its jitter tail, the
existing pool-exhausted behavior is unchanged (the earliest
eligibility instant is what the cooldown error now reports); no
waiting loop was added anywhere.

**Stability.** The roll happens **once, at lock write time**, inside
the two writers (`Repo.LockConnectionRateLimit`,
`Repo.RecordConnectionOAuthFailure`) and is persisted in the same
statement as the park itself. Successive selection checks read the
stored instant and always agree — no per-check re-roll, no flicker,
stable across restarts. A lock written with jitter off (or for a
provider outside the scope) stores a **null** companion, retiring
any roll an older episode left behind; the success/reset clears
(`ClearConnectionRateLimit`, `ClearConnectionSuccessState`,
`ClearConnectionOAuthLock`, `ResetConnectionHealthState`, and the
activation branch of `SetConnectionStatus`) null the companions
alongside their parks. A companion that is not later than its own
park is inert by construction, so a dashboard reset that clears a
park but leaves a companion behind (the reset paths rewrite the
blob field by field) cannot extend a later park: the next lock
write overwrites the companion atomically anyway.

**Parameters (final).**
- Setting: `ProviderStrategy.CooldownJitterSec`
  (`providerStrategies.<provider>.cooldownJitterSec` in the settings
  row, beside the other per-provider strategy fields).
- Unset (the default): the derived window — `rand(0, 10% of the
  cooldown being written)`, capped at 5 minutes. **No floor**: the
  design names no floor for the proportional shape (the 30s figure
  was a fixed-window candidate, not a floor), so short parks get
  proportionally small jitter — a 2s bare-429 backoff rolls within
  0.2s. Rolled with `math/rand/v2`, the jitter source the existing
  precedents use.
- Explicit `0`: jitter off — selectable at the announced expiry,
  exactly the pre-974 behavior.
- Positive `N`: a fixed `rand(0, N seconds)` window replaces the
  derived one.
- Scope: the derived default applies to **antigravity only** (the
  writer resolves the connection's provider and canonicalizes it).
  Another provider gets jitter only when an operator explicitly sets
  a positive value on its own strategy entry — the opt-in door the
  design asked to leave open, with the default blast radius kept at
  one provider. The writer's provider/settings reads are two
  primary-key/settings-row lookups on the lock-write (failure) path;
  the selection hot path gained no query — readers parse the blob
  they already hold.

**Deliberate exclusions.**
- **Per-model locks (`LockConnectionModel`) are NOT jittered.** C as
  decided covers the account-scoped parks behind
  `ConnectionBlockedUntil`. Model locks are written on every
  classified failure — including purely model-scoped errors, where
  the account stays selectable for other models — and are mirrored
  into the speed-layer overlay keyed by the exact announced
  timestamp; the synchronized re-entry C targets is pool-wide
  *account* re-entry at the announced reset instant, and when an
  error is account-scoped the account park written beside the model
  lock carries the jitter. Model locks are the named follow-up if
  per-model re-entry sync ever becomes the observable.
- **The in-memory antigravity quota cache**
  (`chat/antigravity_quota.go`) is NOT jittered. Its blocks are
  model-scoped (same family as the model locks above), and its
  `resetAt` values are live upstream quota readings that each
  refresh replaces wholesale (30s refresh floor) — a stored jitter
  offset would be discarded and re-rolled per refresh, violating
  the roll-once stability requirement. The strike-breaker keeps its
  own semantics.
- **Background refresh keeps reading the raw OAuth park**
  (`ConnectionOAuthLockUntil`). Refresh is a repair path, not
  generation selection: a refresh that succeeds inside the jitter
  tail clears the park early, which is the documented
  `ClearConnectionOAuthLock` behavior ("a repaired credential does
  not stay out of rotation"), and the strike counter keeps keying
  on the raw park exactly as before. Fragment 968's refresh
  *scheduling* jitter is untouched.
- **Quota scoring keeps reading the raw `rateLimitedUntil`**
  (`chat/tokenmaxxing.go` synthesizes its rateLimited quota window
  from the announced reset): it derives a quota window from the
  upstream announcement, it is not an eligibility gate.
- **Fragment 973 is untouched**: no 973 file was modified, pacing
  never reads or writes `isActive`/disabled state, and a disabled
  row is never in the candidate set pacing could affect.

**Files.** `internal/db/accounts_pacing.go` (new: window resolution
+ the write-time roll), `internal/db/accounts_oauth_lock.go`
(`ConnectionBlockedUntil` folds the companions via
`parkEffectiveUntil`; `RecordConnectionOAuthFailure` and
`ClearConnectionOAuthLock` write/clear the OAuth companion),
`internal/db/accounts.go` (`LockConnectionRateLimit`,
`ClearConnectionRateLimit`, `ClearConnectionSuccessState`,
`ResetConnectionHealthState`), `internal/db/dashboard.go`
(`SetConnectionStatus` activation clears the OAuth companion),
`internal/db/settings.go` (the `CooldownJitterSec` field + its
deep-copy in `cloneProviderStrategies`).

**Verification.** `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean on
`internal/db`, `internal/handlers/chat`, `internal/handlers/dashboard`,
`internal/proxy`; `gofmt` clean on all touched files. Direct checks
against the staging PostgreSQL (synthetic connections, removed
after; no test suites run): an antigravity 1h rate-limit lock stored
a companion +10s inside the [expiry, expiry+5m] window and
`ConnectionBlockedUntil` returned exactly the stored companion; a
legacy blob without a companion read back the raw expiry unchanged;
a first-strike OAuth park (5m) stored a companion +15s inside
[expiry, expiry+30s]; a non-antigravity lock stored **no**
companion and read back raw; the clear paths retired both parks
and both companions. Boot smoke: the built binary booted against
the staging database and `GET /api/version` answered 200.

## Antigravity: generation-path ToS detection now disables on every surface

The JS pool post-mortem (2026-11-06) proved the masking mechanism: a
ToS-disabled account keeps answering on the quota/loadCodeAssist path,
so any check that reads quota state reports it healthy while generation
is dead. Detection therefore has to come from generation traffic itself.
This change surveys what ErNor's 5ee02c10 already wired, and closes the
surfaces it missed.

### What already existed (survey, kept as-is)

- Status model: `Repo.DisableConnectionWithReason` sets isActive=0,
  data.status/testStatus="disabled", data.lastError {status, message,
  timestamp}, and appends the appeal form URL to ToS-shaped reasons.
- Chat generic fallback (`fallback.go`, mirrored in `combo.go`): a 403
  whose extracted error text names the ToS phrases disables with the
  verbatim text.
- Background OAuth refresh skips disabled connections at selection and
  again at refresh time; `GetActiveOAuthConnections` excludes them; the
  chat force-refresh refuses inactive rows. Dashboard single-usage fetch
  early-returns the stored error for inactive connections without
  touching Google. Selection queries filter isActive=1 and the disable
  write invalidates the connection cache, so rotation drops the account
  from the moment of disable.
- Quota Tracker and Provider Detail already render the stored error
  with the appeal link (https://forms.gle/hGzM9MEUv2azZsrb9) for
  ToS-shaped messages; the tracker never quota-fetches disabled rows,
  and its per-row reset button renders only for active connections.
- The provider-wide bulk "reset all cooldowns" already skipped
  inactive connections.

### Gaps closed

- **Media generation never disabled.** Image, STT and search handlers
  classified a ToS 403 through the generic rules and parked the account
  on the 24h ToS cooldown, then kept serving it. All three now check
  the shared signature first and disable permanently.
- **One signature, one home.** `providers.LooksLikeToSDisabled`
  (internal/providers/tos_disabled.go): a 403 whose body carries
  TOS_VIOLATION, "disabled in this account", or "violation of (the)
  Terms of Service". Deliberately narrower than the phrase lists it
  replaces at these sites: PERMISSION_DENIED alone is not the signature
  (VALIDATION_REQUIRED carries it), non-403 statuses never are (a 429
  quoting the sentence is a throttle), and quota/loadCodeAssist
  responses are never used as detection input. The native Gemini chat
  path and both fallback chains match it against the raw body in
  addition to their existing extracted-text phrases, so a verdict whose
  message is vague but whose status/reason tokens carry the signature
  still lands.
- **Native chat stored a paraphrase.** gemini_handler.go disabled with
  the canned string "Account disabled for ToS violation"; it now
  stores the verbatim upstream verdict ("Account disabled: " + message,
  status and reason tokens — via `providers.GoogleErrorText` in the
  media lanes, the chat extractor in chat), the same shape the fallback
  path stores, so the dashboard and appeal flow quote Google, not us.
- **The connection probe dialed Google for dead accounts.**
  HandleTestConnection ran the full probe (token refresh +
  loadCodeAssist) on a disabled connection, and persistProbeResult
  could overwrite the disabled verdict with a transient one. The probe
  now returns the stored disabled state without dialing, at both the
  single-test entry and inside testSingleConnection (batch callers),
  and persistProbeResult refuses to write over a stored disabled state.
  Only the stored disabled state is guarded — an operator-toggled-off
  or OAuth-parked (inactive, not disabled) account can still be probed
  manually.
- **Cooldown reset could revive a disabled account.** Bulk
  reset-status with action "cooldown" and an explicit id list (the
  Quota Tracker's per-row reset shape) reactivated the account and
  wiped its verdict, despite the UI intending "disabled accounts are
  never touched". In cooldown mode the handler now skips any inactive
  or stored-disabled connection however it was targeted. The explicit
  full reset (single reset-status, bulk without the cooldown action)
  remains the operator's deliberate reactivation path, as in JS where a
  manual reset-status clears the ToS marker after a successful appeal.

### Residual limits

- Detection is traffic-driven only: an account that is disabled while
  idle is caught on its next generation call, not before. No active
  probing was added (a probe is itself a generation-shaped call against
  an account Google is watching, and the quota path cannot substitute).
- In-band SSE errors after a 200 header are not classified; Google's
  disable verdict is a header-level 403 in every observed case.
- The usage/subscription fetch path can still disable an account when
  its response carries the verdict (pre-existing ErNor behavior); it is
  not relied on for detection and cannot mask a disable, only add one.

## [v1.9.19] - 2026-11-06

# 972 — Antigravity: identity pinned per account (hybrid) + agy scope parity

Ricki's decision (2026-11-06): the router keeps the fragment-969 agy CLI
identity SHAPE, but the identity is PINNED PER ACCOUNT at OAuth time and
never changes for the life of the connection — the JS model's
one-account-one-fixed-identity principle, applied to the CLI identity
instead of the IDE profile. 969's pure runtime derivation (every account
presenting the serving host's live GOOS/GOARCH) is superseded: permanence
per account is the load-bearing property. This fragment also applies the
one CERTAIN delta from fragment 971 (the `openid` scope).

## The pin

- **Storage**: ONE JSON value in the connection's
  `providerSpecificData` under the new key **`antigravityIdentity`**.
  The legacy `clientProfile` value is NOT reused (its ide/cli enum is
  retired); it stays inert as before.
- **Snapshot shape** (`providers.AntigravityIdentity`):
  `{"userAgent": string, "platform": int, "ideVersion": string}` —
  everything that varies by runtime: the full UA string, the
  `loadCodeAssist` platform enum, and the CLI version the UA was built
  from. `LoadCodeAssistMetadata()` derives the numeric metadata
  (`ideType` 9, `pluginType` 2) from the pinned platform.
- **Parsing**: a pin counts only when it parses with a non-empty
  `userAgent` and a non-zero `platform`; anything else reads as
  unpinned.

## Write rules

- **OAuth creation** (`handlers/oauth/antigravity.go`, both the INSERT
  and the re-exchange UPDATE branch): a fresh snapshot of the current
  runtime derivation is stored with the new connection data. On
  re-exchange, an existing VALID pin in the stored data is carried into
  the rewritten data verbatim — re-login never re-pins. Exactly once
  per account lifetime; no other code path mutates an existing pin, and
  there is no UI for it.
- **Lazy backfill**: a connection without a pin is pinned on the first
  identity resolution that has store access:
  - chat: when the handler resolves the connection's data
    (`antigravityConnData`, antigravity connections only);
  - dashboard: `resolveAntigravityIdentity` (usage, models fetch,
    probe).
  The write is `db.Repo.SetConnectionAntigravityIdentity`: a single
  UPDATE whose WHERE clause requires the pin to still be absent
  (first writer wins; verified live against the staging PG, including
  the no-`providerSpecificData` case, where a COALESCE pair creates the
  object). The in-memory copy is updated with the same snapshot, so the
  resolving call itself already serves the pinned identity. A failed
  write is logged and ignored — the next persisting touch retries, and
  every surface derives from the same runtime in the meantime, so there
  is no observable divergence.

## Read rules

- ONE resolver family in the providers package:
  `AntigravityIdentityPinned(psd)` (pin or zero),
  `AntigravityIdentityForPSD(psd)` (pin or runtime),
  `AntigravityRuntimeIdentity()`. Surfaces resolve PER CONNECTION:
  chat forwarding + `ForwardGemini` fallback (the connection's identity
  is resolved once per request and threaded into the translator
  wrappers, so body `userAgent` == header UA), project discovery
  (loadCodeAssist/onboard metadata + UA), quota lanes (refresh/fetch
  carry the UA), media image/search/STT (identity resolved via the
  chat handler's exported accessor), dashboard usage + subscription
  info (metadata from the pin), dashboard models fetch, and the
  connection probe (identity resolved once, reused across its 401
  refresh retry).
- Surfaces with NO connection in scope keep the runtime derivation by
  design: the translator wrappers' default when handed an empty UA,
  and the providers-level helpers themselves
  (`AntigravityLoadCodeAssistMetadata()` now delegates to the runtime
  identity).

## §7 application (fragment 971 verdicts)

- **Scopes — APPLIED (CERTAIN, runtime capture).** The OAuth handler's
  scope list is now agy's captured order: cloud-platform,
  userinfo.email, userinfo.profile, cclog, experimentsandconfigs,
  aicode, `openid`. The only delta vs before is the added `openid` and
  the ordering.
- **Hosts — NO CHANGE.** The endpoint verdict is LIKELY-grade (daily),
  and JS parity keeps discovery/probe on prod; nothing moves on a
  LIKELY.
- **OAuth client — NO CHANGE.** The 971 runtime capture proved agy's
  interactive sign-in uses the router's current 1071 primary client.
  The previously planned flip to the 884354919052 client is
  RECLASSIFIED from a deferred parity step to an open question: its
  serving flow is unknown, and no flip happens unless new evidence
  names that flow. The fragment-970 dual-config rescue slot stays as
  the landing place if a second client is ever proven.

## Residual unknowns (carried from 971, unchanged)

- Whether the `RunLogin` configs carry the identical scope list is
  UNKNOWN (the capture covers the interactive sign-in flow only).
- The endpoint rule stays LIKELY, not CERTAIN (gated behind a completed
  Google sign-in capture).
- `pluginVersion`, `updateChannel`, and `duetProject` remain omitted
  from the loadCodeAssist metadata — unproven, never invented.
- agy's token fallback filename stays uncorroborated; the router stores
  tokens in the DB, so no surface depends on it.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean on providers, db, translator,
  proxy, and handlers (chat, oauth, dashboard, media). Mechanical
  call-site updates in existing tests for the two widened signatures
  (translator wrappers, quota functions); no test suites run.
- Boot smoke vs staging PG (`router9_staging`): `GET /api/version`
  200.
- The backfill UPDATE's SQL chain exercised directly against the
  staging PG in a rolled-back transaction: writes into a row with no
  pre-existing `providerSpecificData`, reads back verbatim, and a
  second write is a no-op (first writer wins).

Completes the remaining open items of the official `agy` v1.5.1 teardown
(`~/workspace/agy-analysis/AGY-IDENTITY-SPEC.md` §7, resolved in place
2026-11-06) and records what each verdict means for this router.
**This fragment intentionally ships no code changes**: the application
target (full-agy parity vs the pinned-per-account hybrid) is awaiting
confirmation, so the deltas below are recorded, not applied. The
fragment-970 dual-config refresher work is untouched.

## Verdicts

- **Endpoint rule — LIKELY `daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`.**
  `main.main` lazy-defaults a package-main endpoint string global to the
  daily literal at three sites (the only default-value use of either host
  literal in the binary); all prod-literal references are

  the global cannot be proven to be the provider's endpoint field, and

  `https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback`, PKCE S256,

  the `RunLogin` configs carry the identical scope list is UNKNOWN.
- **Token file format — informational only.** agy persists via
  `cliFileTokenStorage` (CLI) / `fileTokenStorage` + composite (LS),
  keyring primary, with oauth2.Token JSON field names. The previously
  assumed fallback filename (`oauth_tokens.json`) is NOT corroborated
  by any literal in the binary (only `mcp_oauth_tokens.json` exists).
  No router surface is affected (tokens are stored in the DB).
- **Updater TTL — informational only.** 900 s (15 min), read from the
  freshness helper's immediate `0xd18c2e2800` ns compared against

## Recorded deltas (NOT applied — pending application-target confirmation)

- **OAuth client:** unchanged by this fragment. The runtime capture

## Antigravity OAuth: dual-config refresher — the client swap is now a config flip

Fragment 969 rebased every Antigravity surface onto the real `agy` CLI
identity and left exactly one residual: the OAuth client. `agy` signs in
with its own client (the 884354919052 pair), while this router's
`KnownOAuthConfigs["antigravity"]` still holds the pre-rebase
1071006060591 pair — the pair `agy` itself carries as the secondary
config in its RunLogin. This change builds the full dual-config
architecture that mirrors that RunLogin, so the swap itself is no
longer a code change: it is a one-step flip of the primary slot's
values, whenever the 8843 pair lands.

- `internal/providers/oauth.go` gains `AntigravityLegacyOAuthConfig`,
  a named home for the pre-swap client. It is fenced to one role —
  refresh rescue — and is never used for sign-in or code exchange: the
  sign-in handler continues to seed from `KnownOAuthConfigs` only.
  Today it intentionally holds the same pair as the primary slot: the
  day the primary flips, this slot already holds the client every
  existing account's refresh token was minted under.
- New `internal/proxy/oauth/antigravity.go` registers a custom
  Antigravity refresher (so `RegisterAll` no longer substitutes the
  plain standard one). Selection rules:
  - Refresh is attempted with the PRIMARY config first, exactly as
    before.
  - Exactly ONE rescue attempt under the legacy config runs when —
    and only when — the primary attempt is rejected as a client
    mismatch: HTTP 401, or HTTP 400 whose error body names
    `invalid_client` or `invalid_grant` (Google's answer when a
    refresh token is redeemed under a different client than the one
    that minted it). The classifier is deliberately narrower than
    `providers.IsRefreshGrantDead`: `invalid_request` and friends are
    terminal for the grant itself, not evidence about client
    ownership, and never trigger a rescue.
  - If the rescue also fails, the PRIMARY attempt's error is
    returned, so grant-dead parking and every other caller behavior
    see exactly the error they would have seen with no rescue
    configured.
  - Non-mismatch failures (transport, 5xx, quota) never trigger the
    rescue: they say nothing about which client owns the grant.
  - Skip-when-same-ID: while both slots name the same client (the
    state until the flip), the rescue is skipped rather than resending
    the identical grant under the identical client — so today's wire
    behavior is unchanged.
- Coverage is the `oauth.Refresh` registry, which every Antigravity
  refresh path already funnels through: the background refresher
  (`internal/proxy/oauth/background.go`), the dashboard usage
  credentials refresh (`internal/handlers/dashboard/usage_credentials.go`),
  the connection probe, and the chat force-refresh's first attempt.
  The chat handler's generic fallback after a registry failure (a
  primary-config-only `providers.RefreshToken`, shared by all OAuth
  providers) is unchanged and never touches the legacy config.
- The remaining flip, when the 8843 secret is available: replace the
  primary slot's values with the 884354919052 pair — via the
  `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
  env overrides or the literals in `KnownOAuthConfigs`. Nothing else
  moves: sign-in and code exchange pick the new primary up from the
  same seed, and the rescue slot is already correct for pre-flip
  accounts. If a refresh ever fails under BOTH clients (a revoked
  grant, not a mismatch), the account is parked as grant-dead and
  needs a fresh sign-in — the same consequence as before this change.

## [v1.9.18] - 2026-11-06

## Antigravity identity: rebased from the IDE profile to the real `agy` CLI

Fragment 968 made every Antigravity surface present the identity stored
on the connection — CLI by default, IDE when chosen. That was still two
clients too many: the suspend analysis (docs/ANTIGRAVITY_SUSPEND_ANALYSIS.md
§1) indicted one account wearing several client shapes, and the operator's
direction is to mirror the one client the accounts are actually used
through — the standalone Antigravity CLI (`agy`), torn down from the
official v1.5.1 binary with REA (§13 of the analysis doc). This change
deletes the profile concept and rebases the identity wholesale:

- One definition: `internal/providers/antigravity_identity.go`.
  `AntigravityUserAgent()` builds the UA in agy's runtime grammar —
  `antigravity/cli/1.5.1 (aidev_client; os_type=<runtime GOOS>;
  arch=<runtime GOARCH>; cl=1012564305; auth_method=consumer)` — with
  os/arch from the process runtime, never a hardcoded foreign OS, and
  the changelist agy 1.5.1's own build metadata carries (the old UA
  was a frozen 1.4.0-era Windows capture, cl=1000494485).
  `AntigravityLoadCodeAssistMetadata()` returns the numeric
  ClientMetadata: ideType 9 (ANTIGRAVITY), pluginType 2 (GEMINI),
  ideVersion "1.5.1", ideName "antigravity", platform derived from the
  same runtime OS/arch. pluginVersion, updateChannel and duetProject
  are omitted — the teardown could not establish their values, and an
  invented value would itself be a fingerprint.
- `internal/providers/antigravity_profile.go` is deleted. A
  `clientProfile` value stored on an old connection stays in the data,
  inert and unread; nothing in the tree resolves it any more.
- Every surface consumes the one definition: chat forwarding and the
  ForwardGemini fallback, project discovery (loadCodeAssist +
  onboardUser), the chat quota lanes (which sent a stray
  `antigravity/1.0.0` UA plus an X-Client pair), the translator's chat
  and image wrappers (the body `userAgent` field now equals the header
  UA, as in agy), media image/search/STT (X-Client-Name /
  X-Client-Version removed — the real CLI sends no such pair; body
  `userAgent` aligned), dashboard usage, weekly overlay and
  subscription info (X-Client pair removed, metadata via the shared
  builder), the dashboard models fetch, and the connection probe.
  Hosts are unchanged (daily vs prod exactly as before).
- The connection probe's antigravity branch now sends the numeric
  metadata body and the CLI UA: fragment 968 kept it byte-identical to
  the JS build, but agy parity supersedes JS parity for this provider.
  The gemini-cli probe branch is untouched, and X-Goog-Api-Client
  stays absent from loadCodeAssist (the real client does not send it
  there).
- The OAuth sign-in handler seeds its client from
  providers.KnownOAuthConfigs instead of a duplicated literal, and the
  scope list gains https://www.googleapis.com/auth/aicode — the
  distinctive scope present in every agy CLI auth flow.
- X-Goog-Request-Reason is resolved and deliberately not sent: in agy
  the header is conditional on a host-set runtime string that stays
  empty in the standalone CLI flow, so the real client effectively
  never sends it (the JS build never sends it either).

Open residual — the OAuth client swap is DEFERRED (operator decision):
agy signs in with its 884354919052 client, while this router still
signs in and refreshes with the pre-rebase 1071006060591 client,
restored as the primary in KnownOAuthConfigs. The design is ready to
apply the moment the 8843 client's secret lands in the source: the
8843 config becomes primary, and the 1071 config becomes a fenced
refresh-rescue fallback in a dual-config refresher — new client first,
exactly one legacy attempt on a client-mismatch rejection (401, or 400
naming invalid_client / invalid_grant), the primary error surfaced if
the rescue also fails — because existing accounts' refresh tokens are
bound to the client that minted them. If a refresh ever failed under
both clients, that account would need a fresh sign-in; nothing else
about its data changes. No dual-config refresher exists until then:
one client, one home.

Remaining teardown unknowns (§7 of the identity spec): the endpoint
selection rule (daily vs prod per surface), the exact sign-in scope
list beyond the confirmed aicode scope, the token file format, and
the updater TTL.

## Antigravity safety: one identity per account, account-proxy egress, usage cache

The Antigravity suspend investigation (docs/ANTIGRAVITY_SUSPEND_ANALYSIS.md)
found the Go build presenting several different client identities for the
same account and sending background traffic from the server's own IP —
the two loudest signals distinguishing this router from the real clients
and from the JS build, which stayed unsuspended.

- Per-account identity is now consistent: the profile stored on the
  connection (CLI by default, IDE when chosen) drives the User-Agent on
  chat, media (image/search/STT), dashboard usage (including the weekly
  overlay and subscription-info calls) and the models fetch. The IDE
  profile no longer aliases to the CLI identity (`antigravity/2.23.0`,
  the real IDE app shape). The connection probe is unchanged — its body
  and headers are byte-identical to the JS build.
- Background OAuth refresh and dashboard usage fetches now egress
  through the account's proxy (connection binding first, then the
  provider's strategy pool), falling back to a direct connection only
  when no proxy is bound — the JS build's strictProxy=false semantics —
  instead of always using the server IP.
- GET /api/usage/{id} responses are cached for 55 seconds per
  connection (JS USAGE_RESPONSE_TTL_S parity); ?force=1 bypasses the
  lookup and refreshes the entry.
- Background refresh cadence is de-synchronized: the due list is
  shuffled every tick and the inter-account gap is jittered by +0-50%,
  so the fleet no longer refreshes in the same order on a fixed
  metronome (the code claimed jitter it did not have).
- Routing logs are mirrored to a rotating file
  (<data dir>/logs/routing.log, 20 MiB x 5; AXONROUTER_LOG_FILE
  overrides the path, "off" disables) so incidents can be analysed
  from disk afterwards.
- The quota tracker gains a name/email search (server-side `search`
  parameter on /api/providers/client) and cooldown reset actions —
  per-account and reset-all — wired to the bulk reset's cooldown
  action, which never touches disabled accounts. The provider detail
  page no longer auto-fetches usage for every connection on open;
  quotas load on demand via its Load quotas button.

## Dashboard E2E: a database-backed suite, gated like one

The CI test job's last red step: Dashboard E2E failed with "gateway
exited during boot with code 1" (nineteen times — once per file). It
was masked until now because the job used to die earlier, at the
svelte-check ratchet.

Root cause: the E2E harness boots the real gateway, and since P4 the
gateway's database is PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL — there is no file
database to fall back to (the harness header still describes the
removed SQLite setup). CI configures no database, so the binary exits
at boot. Under the owner's rule (fragment 966: database-backed tests
skip when no database is configured) this suite is a database-backed
surface and is gated the same way:

- The CI step now runs only when the E2E_DATABASE_URL repository
  variable names a reachable scratch PostgreSQL, passed to the suite
  as DATABASE_URL. Unset (the default) → the step is skipped and the
  job stays green.
- The harness names the requirement up front when no DSN is present,
  replacing the opaque boot-exit error with the actual cause.

## Database-backed tests skip when no database is configured (owner rule)

Owner order (2026-11-06): "test yang butuh db itu di skip aja" — a
test that needs a database should skip, not fail, when no database is
configured. CI therefore provisions no database again: the postgres
service fragments 953/965 added to the integration job is removed,
and the job returns to its plain shape.

- dbtest gains a sentinel, ErrNoDatabase, returned (wrapped) by
  BaseDSN when neither INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL nor DATABASE_URL is
  set. It is deliberately distinct from a configured database that
  fails to connect or provision — that stays a failure.
- The integration harness skips on ErrNoDatabase (t.Skip) instead of
  failing at provision; bootfx's TestMain reports the skip and exits
  clean, since every test in that package needs the boot database.
- Wherever a DSN IS configured the suite runs in full, unchanged —
  verified both ways locally: no env → SKIP + package ok; env set →
  the same tests pass.

## CI integration job: SASL auth failure — the password existed twice and disagreed

**Symptom.** The first CI run with the PostgreSQL service (fragment
953) failed all 291 integration tests at 0.01s each:
"password authentication failed for user postgres (SQLSTATE 28P01)".

**Root cause.** Fragment 953's workflow carried the scratch
database's password in two places — the service container's
POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL — and the two
values were different strings. The service initialized with one, the
tests connected with the other. Local verification could not catch
it: the local scratch database predates the workflow and its
password lives in a single env file.

**Fix.** The duplicated value is deleted rather than synchronized.
The ephemeral, runner-local scratch database now uses
POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust and a passwordless DSN — there is
nothing left to disagree. The job comment records the reasoning.
Also: the test step's timeout rises 10m → 25m; the suite measured
646s locally WITHOUT -race on a loaded 4-vCPU VM, so 10m under
-race was never a safe ceiling for a green run.

**Verification.** The exact failure string comes from the CI run's
own log (job 127448646859); the fix removes the mechanism (two
values) rather than patching one value against the other. The
follow-up CI run on main is the end-to-end proof.

CI's test job failed its Svelte check step: "svelte-check errors

The baseline now records the verified current count (80), written by

## [v1.9.17] - 2026-11-06

## MiniMax Code: a Claude client's reply is no longer translated into OpenAI shape

**Symptom.** A /v1/messages client routed to minimax-code received an
OpenAI-shaped body (no `type: "message"`, no Claude content blocks) in
answer to a Claude Messages reply from the mavis upstream —
TestMiniMaxCodeClaudeWire in the integration suite.

**Root cause.** A flag-polarity collision. The Claude response helpers
read TranslateResp in their convention (true = the client speaks
Claude → pass through; false = OpenAI client → translate). The chat
layer's translateResponse has the opposite meaning on the /v1/messages
lane: it is false for Claude-native providers precisely because no
translation was expected. ForwardMinimaxCode used to ignore the flag
for Claude clients (raw relay); a later change routed every reply
through the helpers, so the messages lane's false was obeyed as
"translate to OpenAI" and Claude clients got chat.completion JSON.

**Fix.** ForwardMinimaxCode hands the helpers the flag in their own
convention: `req.TranslateResp = req.ClaudeClient` before dispatch.
ClaudeClient is derived from the endpoint itself at both
request-construction sites, so it cannot drift from the client's
actual format. The /v1/chat/completions lane keeps the translation
the earlier change was for; the /v1/messages lane passes through —
now through the helpers, so tool decloaking applies there too (the
old raw relay skipped it).

**Verification.** TestMiniMaxCodeClaudeWire (and the global-site and
auth-refusal companions) pass against a live PostgreSQL through the
real router; previously the wire test failed on the reply shape.

## GET /api/connections: the unfiltered list returns connections again

**Symptom.** GET /api/connections without a `?provider=` filter
returned `[]` with a 200 — visible in the integration suite
(TestConnectionLifecycle, TestConnectionNameConflictIsRefused: a
just-created connection "is not in the list []") and in the dashboard
itself, whose unfiltered callers (App boot, the add-from-link modal)
silently received nothing.

**Root cause.** A perf guard (commit 68e94eb3) short-circuited the
handler to an empty list when no provider filter was given, to avoid
dumping a very large connections table. The guard changed the
endpoint's contract instead of its cost profile, and every caller
that relied on the upstream list shape broke without an error.

**Fix.** The short-circuit is removed: the handler again serves
GetProviderConnections for the filter as given (empty filter = all
connections), with the existing secret-stripping sanitizer unchanged.
The aggregate views that motivated the guard read /api/providers/stats;
the handler comment records the reasoning so the guard is not
reintroduced.

**Verification.** The integration lifecycle and name-conflict tests,
which failed against the guarded handler, pass against a live
PostgreSQL through the real router.

**Symptom.** Every release run failed its `docker` job at "Log in to

**Root cause.** The job was an upstream leftover twice over: it pushed

(ghcr.io/rmz17x/axonrouter-go) from the Publish Docker Image workflow,

**Fix.** The Docker Hub job is deleted from release.yml, along with

coordinate, and the prerelease banner's pull line uses it with the
full tag (GHCR tags keep the `v`). One trade-off, recorded: the
removed job built linux/arm64 as well as amd64; the GHCR workflow
builds amd64 — arm64 users are served by the native release binaries.

MediaProviderDetail rendered the NoAuth proxy card for noAuth

## Proxy resolution readout: a binding that resolves to nothing is now visible

Every proxy-binding bug in this area shared one shape: the dashboard
showed a selection as set while the resolver matched zero pools and
requests silently went direct. The fix is a readout that shows the
resolution itself, next to the controls that set it.

- New read-only endpoint GET /api/providers/proxy-resolution?id=<provider>
  (registered in both route tables). It derives the selector from the
  stored provider strategy exactly as the chat resolver does — same
  strategy-key walk (id, alias, canonical), same sentinels, same legacy
  bare-type heal — and matches candidates with the production
  Repo.ActivePoolsByTarget. It reports the binding kind (group / type /
  pool / rotation / direct / none), the selector, the active candidate
  pools, and whether it resolves at all. A small exported
  db.IsKnownProxyType wrapper keeps the heal's type set in one place.
- A shared ProxyResolutionNote component renders one line: the resolved
  pool names and count, or an amber warning — "matches no active pool —
  requests will go direct" — when the selection resolves to zero. It
  sits under the provider Proxy Lock (connections detail) and inside
  the NoAuth proxy card, refreshing after every save.
- While wiring the card: its save now deletes both rotation spellings,
  not only rotateStrategy. The stored rotateStrategy key is the live
  one (the settings parser maps it onto the resolver's
  ProxyRotateStrategy field); a stray proxyRotateStrategy key is never
  parsed back, but leaving it would keep a phantom setting on display.
  A card save expresses the complete group/type/none choice, so
  neither spelling may survive it.

Three unit tests had drifted from deliberate behaviour and failed in CI:
